## File: docs/getting-started/installation.md

````markdown
# Installation

## Requirements

- Python 3.10 or newer
- `git` on the `PATH`
- Optional: the GitHub CLI `gh`, for `release --pr` and pull request titles in
  the changelog

## As a command line tool

```bash
# Run without installing
uvx gitversioned version
pipx run gitversioned version

# Or install it
uv tool install gitversioned
pipx install gitversioned
pip install gitversioned
```

### Verify the installation

```console
$ gitversioned --version
gitversioned v0.4.0
$ gitversioned check
```

`gitversioned check` reports whether the repository can give a trustworthy
version and lists the files that would be stamped.

## As a build dependency

A Python project does not install gitversioned by hand. It lists it in
`build-system.requires` and the build front end installs it into the isolated
build:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

See the [Hatchling](../guides/hatchling.md), [Setuptools](../guides/setuptools.md)
and [Maturin](../guides/maturin.md) guides.

## Container image

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo ghcr.io/markurtz/git-versioned:latest \
  gitversioned version
```

## From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned.git
cd git-versioned
uv sync
uv run gitversioned --version
```

## Upgrading and uninstalling

```bash
uv tool upgrade gitversioned     # or: pipx upgrade gitversioned
uv tool uninstall gitversioned   # or: pipx uninstall gitversioned
```

Upgrading from 0.3? See the [Migration Guide](../guides/migration.md).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                                         | Fix                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The version is `0.1.0...` in CI, or exit code 3 | The clone is shallow. Set `fetch-depth: 0` on `actions/checkout`. |
| A GitHub source tarball builds as `0.1.0`       | Run `gitversioned init` once and commit the two files.            |
| `settings found in two homes`                   | Keep the settings in one file.                                    |
| `release --pr` says `gh` is missing             | Install the GitHub CLI and set `GH_TOKEN` in CI.                  |
````

## File: docs/getting-started/quickstart.md

````markdown
# Quick Start

Five minutes from an empty repository to a planned release.

## 1. Print the version

```console
$ cd my-project
$ uvx gitversioned version
0.1.0.dev20261125+abc1234
```

With no tags yet the version starts from the fallback `0.1.0`. Tag a release
and it follows the tag:

```console
$ git tag v1.0.0
$ gitversioned version
1.0.0
```

## 2. Check the setup

```console
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tags, latest v1.0.0
ok    targets       Cargo.toml, package.json, src/my_project/version.py
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
```

The `targets` line lists every file gitversioned found a version in. Run
`gitversioned init` once to clear the archive warning.

## 3. Wire up the build

For a Python project, let the build read the version from git:

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "my-project"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "gitversioned"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]
```

For Rust, npm, Helm and container builds, stamp the manifests before building:

```console
$ gitversioned version --write
1.0.1.dev20261125+abc1234
  Cargo.toml    1.0.1-dev.20261125+abc1234
  package.json  1.0.1-dev.20261125+abc1234
```

## 4. Commit with Conventional Commits

```console
$ git commit -m "feat(core): add streaming parser"
$ git commit -m "fix(cli): exit code on empty input"
$ gitversioned check --commits v1.0.0..HEAD
ok    commits  2 commits
```

## 5. Plan the release

```console
$ gitversioned release
release   1.1.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.0.0)
tag       v1.1.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, Cargo.toml, package.json

## 1.1.0 - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **core**: add streaming parser

### Fixed

- **cli**: exit code on empty input

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.
```

`gitversioned release --pr` opens the release pull request with exactly that
content. After it merges, `gitversioned release --tag` tags the merge.

## Next

- [Workflows](workflows.md): the common end-to-end stories.
- [Command Line Guide](../guides/cli.md): every option, with output.
- [Configuration Guide](../guides/configuration.md): the twelve settings.
````

## File: docs/getting-started/workflows.md

````markdown
# Workflows

The common stories, end to end.

## A build that always has the right version

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- run: pipx run build
```

With gitversioned in `build-system.requires`, a tag build is `1.2.0` and every
other build is a development version such as `1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234`.

## Every manifest in step

```bash
gitversioned version --write
cargo build --release --locked
npm pack
docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(gitversioned version --standard semver)" .
```

One command stamps `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `package.json`, `Chart.yaml`,
`CITATION.cff` and the Dockerfile label, each in its own spelling.

## A reviewed release

1. Pull requests merge to `main` with Conventional Commit titles, checked by
   `gitversioned check "$TITLE"`.
1. On every push to `main`, `gitversioned release --pr` opens or updates the
   release pull request: the changelog section and the stamped manifests.
1. A maintainer reviews, edits the changelog if needed and merges.
1. `gitversioned release --tag` tags the merge, and the tag starts the publish
   jobs.

The full workflow files are in the
[GitHub Workflows Guide](../guides/github-workflows.md).

## A release candidate

Add the label `release:rc` to the release pull request. It becomes
`release: v1.5.0-rc.1`; each further merge and tag gives `rc.2`, `rc.3`. Remove
the label to release `1.5.0`, whose changelog section replaces the candidates'.

## Nightly builds

```bash
GITVERSIONED__TYPE=nightly python -m build       # Python: the build hook
gitversioned version --write --type nightly      # Cargo, npm and other manifests
```

A nightly is the next release with the date, such as `1.5.0.dev20261125`, and
has no commit hash, so package indexes accept it. The build plugins take no
flags, so a Python build reads the type from `GITVERSIONED__TYPE`.

## One package of a monorepo

```toml
[packages.web]
path = "packages/web"
tag = "web-v{version}"
```

```bash
gitversioned version -p web
gitversioned release -p web --pr
```

The package is versioned from its own tags and only the commits that touch its
folder count.
````

## File: docs/guides/api.md

````markdown
# Python API Guide

Everything the command line does is available from Python. The top-level
package exports the stable surface.

| Name                               | What it is                                            |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_version(root, standard=)`     | The version of a project as text.                     |
| `load_config(start)`               | The validated settings for a project.                 |
| `resolve(config, ...)`             | The resolved version with its source, tag and commit. |
| `stamp(config, resolved, ...)`     | Write the version into every target.                  |
| `plan_release(config, ...)`        | The next release: version, tag, changelog section.    |
| `Version`                          | A version that prints as PEP 440 or SemVer.           |
| `GitVersionedError` and subclasses | Errors, each with the exit code the CLI would use.    |

## Get the version

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
from gitversioned import get_version

print(get_version())  # 1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
print(get_version(standard="semver"))  # 1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
print(get_version("path/to/project"))
```

## Resolve with detail

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
from gitversioned import load_config, resolve

config = load_config()
resolved = resolve(config)

print(resolved.version.pep440())  # 1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
print(resolved.type)  # dev, nightly or release
print(resolved.source)  # tag, archive, metadata, pin or fallback
print(resolved.tag, resolved.distance, resolved.sha)
print(resolved.warnings)

nightly = resolve(config, build_type="nightly")
pinned = resolve(config, pin="2.0.0")
```

## Stamp files

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
from gitversioned import load_config, resolve, stamp

config = load_config()
for change in stamp(config, resolve(config), dry_run=True):
    print(change.path, change.old, "->", change.new)
```

Each `Change` has `path`, `old`, `new`, `diff`, `commit` and `written`.

## Plan a release

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
from gitversioned import NothingToReleaseError, load_config, plan_release

try:
    plan = plan_release(load_config(), use_github=False)
except NothingToReleaseError:
    print("nothing to release")
else:
    print(plan.version.pep440(), plan.tag, plan.level)
    print(plan.section)  # the changelog section, as Markdown
```

## Work with versions

`Version` needs no repository, so it is useful on its own for parsing,
comparing and converting.

```python
from gitversioned import Version

version = Version.parse("1.2.0-rc.1")
print(version.pep440())
print(version.semver())
print(version.is_final)
print(version.bump("minor").pep440())
print(Version.try_parse("not a version"))

names = ["1.2.0", "1.2.0rc1", "1.2.0.dev1", "1.1.9"]
print(sorted(names, key=lambda name: Version.parse(name).sort_key()))
```

```
1.2.0rc1
1.2.0-rc.1
False
1.3.0
None
['1.1.9', '1.2.0.dev1', '1.2.0rc1', '1.2.0']
```

## Errors

| Error                     | Exit code | Raised when                                     |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `CheckFailedError`        | 1         | A check failed.                                 |
| `NothingToReleaseError`   | 1         | No commit since the last release calls for one. |
| `ConfigError`             | 2         | Settings are invalid or live in two homes.      |
| `EnvironmentProblemError` | 3         | Git or `gh` cannot give a trustworthy answer.   |

All of them derive from `GitVersionedError`.

## Logging

gitversioned logs through Loguru and is silent as a library: importing it
disables its logger, as Loguru advises for libraries. Turn it on with
`logger.enable("gitversioned")` to send its messages to your own handlers, or
get the same output as the command line:

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
from gitversioned.logging import configure_logging

configure_logging(1)  # -1 errors only, 0 warnings, 1 info, 2 debug
```
````

## File: docs/guides/cli.md

````markdown
# Command Line Guide

`gitversioned` has three commands, one per job, and an optional setup step.

| Command   | Job                                                                |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `version` | Print the version, print the next one, or stamp it into the files. |
| `check`   | Validate the repository setup, a title, a commit range or a tag.   |
| `release` | Plan a release, open the release pull request, tag the merge.      |
| `init`    | Optional: add the archive file and wire up the build backend.      |

Every command takes the same shared options.

| Option              | Meaning                                             |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `-C`, `--root DIR`  | Run as if started in `DIR`.                         |
| `-p`, `--package N` | Act on one package from `[packages]`.               |
| `--json`            | Machine-readable output on stdout, errors included. |
| `-v`, `-vv`         | More detail on stderr.                              |
| `-q`, `--quiet`     | Errors only.                                        |

Results go to stdout and everything else goes to stderr, so
`VERSION=$(gitversioned version)` is always safe.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success.                                                                                      |
| 1    | A check failed, or there is nothing to release.                                               |
| 2    | Wrong usage or invalid configuration.                                                         |
| 3    | The environment cannot give a trustworthy answer (shallow clone in CI, no git, `gh` missing). |

______________________________________________________________________

## `version`

```text
gitversioned version [VERSION] [--next] [--bump LEVEL] [--pre KIND]
                     [--type TYPE] [--standard STD]
                     [--write] [--dry-run] [--explain]
```

### Print the version of this checkout

```console
$ gitversioned version
1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
$ gitversioned version --type nightly
1.5.0.dev20261125
```

On a release tag the output is the tag's version. After the tag it is a
development version: the next patch, the commit date and the short commit hash.
A changed tracked file adds `.dirty`. The default spelling is PEP 440 when the
project has a `pyproject.toml` with a `[project]` table, and SemVer otherwise.

### Print the next release

```console
$ gitversioned version --next
1.5.0
$ gitversioned version --next --pre rc
1.5.0rc1
$ gitversioned version --next --bump major
2.0.0
```

`--next` reads the Conventional Commit subjects since the last release. It exits
with code 1 when no commit since then calls for a release.

### See why

```console
$ gitversioned version --explain
version   1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
type      dev
current   1.4.0  (tag v1.4.0, 60439dc, 2 commits since)
why       minor: 1 patch, 1 minor
  patch   fix(cli): exit code on empty input
  minor   feat(core): add streaming parser
note      base 1.4.0 from tag v1.4.0
config    .config/gitversioned.toml  (6 keys set, 8 defaults)
```

### Stamp the files

```console
$ gitversioned version --write
1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
  CITATION.cff            1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  Dockerfile              1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  charts/demo/Chart.yaml  1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  crates/cli/Cargo.toml   1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  crates/core/Cargo.toml  1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  src/demo/version.py     1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc
  Cargo.lock              1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
  docs/install.md         1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc
```

Each file gets the spelling its ecosystem expects. `--dry-run` prints a unified
diff and changes nothing. Stamping never makes the tree count as dirty: a file
whose only change is its version is ignored when the version is resolved again.

Pass a `VERSION` to use that version instead of resolving one, for example
`gitversioned version 2.0.0 --write`.

### JSON

```console
$ gitversioned version --json
{
  "version": "1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc",
  "pep440": "1.4.1.dev20261125+60439dc",
  "semver": "1.4.1-dev.20261125+60439dc",
  "type": "dev",
  "source": "tag",
  "tag": "v1.4.0",
  "distance": 2,
  "sha": "60439dc",
  "dirty": false,
  "warnings": [],
  "written": []
}
```

______________________________________________________________________

## `check`

```text
gitversioned check [TITLE] [--commits RANGE] [--tag NAME] [--file PATH] [--warn]
```

### The repository setup

```console
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        .config/gitversioned.toml
ok    git           full history, 1 release tags, latest v1.4.0
ok    targets       CITATION.cff, Dockerfile, charts/demo/Chart.yaml, ...
ok    scopes        core, cli, web, chart, docs, deps
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

Problems that only warn on a laptop fail in CI (when the `CI` environment
variable is set), with exit code 3. The usual one is a shallow clone: set
`fetch-depth: 0` on `actions/checkout`.

### A pull request title or commit message

```console
$ gitversioned check "feat(core): add a thing"
ok
$ gitversioned check "added a thing"
fail  title  'added a thing' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, ...
$ gitversioned check --file .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG
$ gitversioned check --commits origin/main..HEAD
ok    commits  2 commits
```

`--file` reads the first line of a file, which is what a `commit-msg` hook
passes. `--warn` reports problems as `warn` and still exits 0, which suits a
hook that should only advise.

### A tag name

```console
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.5.0
ok    tag  1.5.0, newer than v1.4.0
```

The tag must match the template and be newer than the last release. If it
exists already, it must point at `HEAD`. When the project has a changelog, it
must have the version's `## [1.5.0]` section. Use this in a workflow that runs
when a tag is pushed, or before tagging by hand; `release --tag` runs the same
checks.

______________________________________________________________________

## `release`

```text
gitversioned release [VERSION] [--bump LEVEL] [--pre KIND] [--write] [--pr] [--tag]
```

A release has three stages. Without a flag the command only shows the plan.

### Plan

```console
$ gitversioned release
release   1.5.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.4.0)
tag       v1.5.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff, Dockerfile, charts/demo/Chart.yaml, crates/cli/Cargo.toml, crates/core/Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, docs/install.md

## [1.5.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **core**: add streaming parser

### Fixed

- **cli**: exit code on empty input

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.
```

### `--write`: update the working tree

Writes the changelog section and stamps every committed target. Nothing is
committed, so this is the stage to use when you make the release commit
yourself.

### `--pr`: open or update the release pull request

Rebuilds the branch `release/next` from the current commit with one commit
titled `release: v1.5.0`, pushes it, and opens a pull request labelled
`release`, or updates the one already open. The pull request body is the
changelog section. Run it on every push to the release branch and the pull
request always shows what the next release will be. It refuses to run on any
other branch, and exits with code 1 when `HEAD` is a merged release commit that
is not tagged yet, so it never reopens a release that is waiting for
`release --tag`. It needs the GitHub CLI
`gh`, signed in (`GH_TOKEN` in CI).

Add the label `release:rc` to the pull request to make it a release candidate.
Add `release:major`, `release:minor` or `release:patch` to a merged pull request
to override the level its title would give.

### `--tag`: tag the merged release

Run on the `branch` setting's branch (`main` by default) right after the release
pull request merges. It reads the
tag from the release commit's subject, checks it is newer than the last
release, creates it and pushes it. Pass a `VERSION` to tag `HEAD` by hand.
Either way it runs the checks of `check --tag` first, so a version without its
changelog section is never tagged.

### Choosing the version

The first of these that is set decides:

1. The `VERSION` argument.
1. `--bump major|minor|patch`.
1. `GITVERSIONED__BUMP` in the environment (a level or a version).
1. A `release:major|minor|patch` label on a pull request merged since the last
   final release.
1. The commits since the last release.

______________________________________________________________________

## `init`

```console
$ gitversioned init
wrote  .git_archival.txt
edit   .gitattributes          + .git_archival.txt  export-subst
```

Adds the two things a repository needs for a version to survive a source
tarball from GitHub, and adds `[tool.hatch.version] source = "gitversioned"` to
a Hatchling project that does not have it yet. It only creates files or appends
to them. Nothing else in gitversioned depends on it.

______________________________________________________________________

## Recipes

### Git hook for commit messages

```bash
# .git/hooks/commit-msg
gitversioned check --file "$1"
```

### Build a container with the right version

```bash
gitversioned version --write
docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(gitversioned version --standard semver)" .
```

### One package in a monorepo

```bash
gitversioned version -p web
gitversioned release -p web --pr
```
````

## File: docs/guides/concepts.md

````markdown
# Concepts

## One version, two spellings

gitversioned keeps one version per checkout and prints it the way each
ecosystem expects.

| Build       | PEP 440 (Python)                  | SemVer (Rust, npm, Helm, OCI)      |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Release     | `1.2.0`                           | `1.2.0`                            |
| Pre-release | `1.2.0rc1`                        | `1.2.0-rc.1`                       |
| Development | `1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234`       | `1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234`       |
| Nightly     | `1.3.0.dev20261125`               | `1.3.0-nightly.20261125`           |
| Dirty tree  | `1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234.dirty` | `1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234.dirty` |

A development version is the next patch after the last release, dated with the
commit date so the same commit always gives the same version. A nightly has no
hash, so it can be uploaded to a package index. The hash is the first seven
characters of the commit, lengthened only in the rare case where those would be
all digits with a leading zero, which Python packaging tools would renumber.

## Where the version comes from

The first source that answers wins:

1. **A pin.** A `VERSION` argument, `GITVERSIONED__VERSION`, or
   `version = "1.2.3"` in the settings.
1. **Git tags.** The highest release tag reachable from `HEAD` that matches the
   tag template, plus the number of commits since.
1. **The archive file.** `.git_archival.txt`, filled in by `git archive`, for
   source tarballs downloaded from GitHub. Files written for setuptools-scm are
   read too.
1. **Package metadata.** `PKG-INFO` in an unpacked sdist.
1. **The fallback.** `0.1.0` unless configured, with a warning.

A tag that looks like a version but does not match the tag template, such as
`1.2.0` when the template is `v{version}`, is ignored with a warning that names
it. The date in a development or nightly version is the commit's date, so a
rebuild gives the same version; `date = "build"` uses the build time, which
honours `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` for reproducible builds.

There are no version files to keep in sync and no version committed between
releases. A tag is the only thing that makes a release.

## Warn on a laptop, fail in CI

When the answer cannot be trusted (a shallow clone with no tag in reach, no git
history at all) gitversioned warns and uses the fallback on a developer
machine. In CI, detected by the `CI` environment variable, the same situation
exits with code 3 so a wrong version is never published.

## How the next version is chosen

`version --next` and `release` read the Conventional Commit subjects since the
last release.

| Commit                                                            | Level |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| `feat!: ...` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer                       | major |
| `feat: ...`                                                       | minor |
| `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `build`, `revert`, `deprecate` | patch |
| `chore`, `ci`, `test`, `release`, merge commits                   | none  |

Below 1.0.0 every level shifts down one, and the plan says so (`minor, a patch
below 1.0.0`): a breaking change is a minor bump and
a feature is a patch bump. An explicit `--bump` is taken as written.

## Stamping

`version --write` puts the version into every target with scoped text edits.
Only the characters of the version change; comments, ordering, quoting and line
endings are kept. Because a stamped manifest differs from git only in its
version, gitversioned does not count it as a dirty tree, so builds that stamp
first and resolve later agree.

## The release flow

```text
commits on main ──► gitversioned release --pr ──► release pull request
                                                    │  review, edit, merge
                                                    ▼
                    gitversioned release --tag ──► tag v1.5.0 ──► publish jobs
```

The release pull request holds one commit: the changelog section and the
stamped manifests. It is rebuilt on every push to the release branch, so it
always shows what the next release would be. Merging it is the decision to
release; tagging the merge is what makes the version.

## The changelog

Each release gets a `## [1.5.0] - 2026-11-25` section with Keep a Changelog
kinds (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security), and the scope in
bold before each entry. `chore`, `ci`, `test` and `release` commits are left
out unless they are breaking. Lines written by hand under `## [Unreleased]`
join the new section and `[Unreleased]` is left empty, so a project can keep
notes there between releases. When `gh` is available, the pull
request title replaces a squash commit's subject, and a `## Changelog` block in
a pull request body replaces the generated entry. A final release takes over
the entries of its release candidates and replaces their sections.
````

## File: docs/guides/configuration.md

````markdown
# Configuration Guide

gitversioned works with no configuration. Everything below is optional, and the
whole surface is twelve settings, a list of extra files and a table of
packages.

## Where settings live

Settings live in exactly one of these places, searched in this order from the
folder the command runs in up to the repository root:

| Home                        | Table                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.config/gitversioned.toml` | The whole file                                                           |
| `gitversioned.toml`         | The whole file                                                           |
| `pyproject.toml`            | `[tool.gitversioned]`                                                    |
| `Cargo.toml`                | `[workspace.metadata.gitversioned]` or `[package.metadata.gitversioned]` |
| `package.json`              | `"gitversioned"`                                                         |
| `setup.cfg`                 | `[tool:gitversioned]`                                                    |

Two homes in the same folder is an error that names both, so a setting can
never be silently shadowed. An unknown key is also an error, and it names the
nearest valid key.

## The settings

| Key         | Default                | What it does                                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`   | `"auto"`               | A pinned version, or `auto` to resolve from git.                                 |
| `fallback`  | `"0.1.0"`              | The base version before the first tag exists.                                    |
| `tag`       | `"v{version}"`         | The tag template; also how release tags are recognised.                          |
| `annotated` | `false`                | Create annotated tags that carry the changelog section.                          |
| `branch`    | `"main"`               | The branch releases are cut from and release pull requests target.               |
| `dev`       | `"patch"`              | The base of a development build: `patch`, `minor`, `major` or `next`.            |
| `nightly`   | `"next"`               | The base of a nightly build; `next` is the next release from commits.            |
| `date`      | `"commit"`             | The date in dev and nightly versions: `commit` (reproducible) or `build`.        |
| `local`     | `true`                 | Add `+<hash>` to development builds.                                             |
| `changelog` | `"CHANGELOG.md"`       | The changelog file, or `false` to turn it off.                                   |
| `types`     | The twelve types below | The commit types `check` accepts.                                                |
| `scopes`    | `[]` (any scope)       | The allowed scopes. An entry ending in `.toml` is a file whose table names are scopes, so `[".config/blocks.toml", "deps"]` mixes both. |

The default types are `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`,
`build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`, `deprecate` and `release`.

### Example: every setting

```toml
# .config/gitversioned.toml
version = "auto"
fallback = "0.1.0"
tag = "v{version}"
annotated = false
branch = "main"
dev = "patch"
nightly = "next"
date = "commit"
local = true
changelog = "CHANGELOG.md"
types = ["feat", "fix", "perf", "refactor", "docs", "test", "build", "ci", "chore", "revert", "deprecate", "release"]
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]
```

The same settings in the other homes:

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.gitversioned]
tag = "v{version}"
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]
```

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[workspace.metadata.gitversioned]
tag = "v{version}"
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]
```

```json
{
  "name": "my-package",
  "gitversioned": {
    "tag": "v{version}",
    "scopes": ["core", "cli", "docs"]
  }
}
```

```ini
# setup.cfg
[tool:gitversioned]
tag = v{version}
scopes = ["core", "cli", "docs"]
```

## Targets: the files that get stamped

Discovery finds these files on its own, among the files git tracks:

| File                   | What is stamped                                                                                             | Spelling |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `pyproject.toml`       | `project.version`, when it is static                                                                        | PEP 440  |
| `<package>/version.py` | Generated, when the build uses gitversioned and the version is dynamic                                      | PEP 440  |
| `Cargo.toml`           | `package.version` or `workspace.package.version`, and the versions of path dependencies on workspace crates | SemVer   |
| `Cargo.lock`           | The entries of the workspace crates                                                                         | SemVer   |
| `package.json`         | `version`                                                                                                   | SemVer   |
| `tauri.conf.json`      | `version`                                                                                                   | SemVer   |
| `Chart.yaml`           | `version` and `appVersion`                                                                                  | SemVer   |
| `CITATION.cff` (root)  | `version`, and `date-released` on a release; both are added when missing                                    | SemVer   |
| `Dockerfile`, `Containerfile` | The `org.opencontainers.image.version` label, unless it is a `$VARIABLE`                             | SemVer   |

In a repository with several `package.json` files, a dependency of one package
on another is stamped too, keeping its operator (`^`, `~`, `=`); `workspace:`
and `catalog:` references are left alone. A private `package.json` with no
`version`, such as a workspace root, is not a target.

Files under `node_modules`, `target`, `dist`, `build`, `site`, `examples`,
`tests`, `test`, `testdata`, `fixtures`, `vendor` and `third_party` are left
alone, and so are manifests that say they are never released: a
`pyproject.toml` with the `Private :: Do Not Upload` classifier and a
cargo-fuzz harness (`cargo-fuzz = true`). Edits are scoped text edits: only the version value changes, so
comments, key order, quoting and line endings survive.

List any other file with `[[targets]]`:

```toml
# A value in a TOML, JSON or YAML file, by dotted key
[[targets]]
path = "deploy/values.yaml"
key = "image.tag"

# Any text file, by a regular expression with a `version` group
[[targets]]
path = "docs/install.md"
pattern = 'my-tool@(?P<version>[0-9][^\s`]*)'

# A file discovery would skip, or one that should not be committed
[[targets]]
path = "examples/demo/package.json"
commit = false
```

| Key       | Meaning                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`    | The file, relative to the project root. Required.                                                                |
| `key`     | Dotted path of the value in a TOML, JSON or YAML file.                                                           |
| `pattern` | Regular expression with a `version` group. Not together with `key`.                                              |
| `commit`  | Whether the release pull request commits the file. Defaults to true for manifests and false for generated files. |

## Packages: more than one version in a repository

```toml
[packages.core]
path = "crates/core"              # follows the repository version

[packages.web]
path = "packages/web"
tag = "web-v{version}"            # its own tags, version and release pull request
```

| Key    | Meaning                                                                |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path` | The package folder, relative to the project root. Required.            |
| `tag`  | A tag template. Without it the package follows the repository version. |

A package with its own `tag` is versioned from its own tags, counts only the
commits that touch its folder, and is left out of the repository's own version
and stamping. Use `-p NAME` on any command to act on it. The package names are
added to the allowed scopes.

## Environment overrides

Any setting can be overridden with `GITVERSIONED__<KEY>`. Lists and booleans
are written as JSON. An unknown `GITVERSIONED__` variable is ignored with a
warning, since the environment is shared with other tools and older releases.

```bash
GITVERSIONED__VERSION=1.2.3 python -m build       # pin the version for one build
GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false gitversioned version    # no +hash, e.g. for TestPyPI
GITVERSIONED__TAG='release-{version}' gitversioned version
GITVERSIONED__SCOPES='["core","cli"]' gitversioned check "feat(core): x"
GITVERSIONED__BUMP=minor gitversioned release     # a level or an exact version
GITVERSIONED__TYPE=nightly python -m build        # release, dev or nightly
```

`GITVERSIONED__BUMP` and `GITVERSIONED__TYPE` are not settings: they stand in
for `--bump` and `--type`. `GITVERSIONED__TYPE` is the only way to pick the
build type inside a build backend, since the build plugins take no flags.

`gitversioned version --explain` lists how many keys were set and where the
settings were read from.

## What is not configurable

These are fixed on purpose, so every repository behaves the same way.

- **Bump rules.** A breaking change is major, `feat` is minor, every other
  releasable type is patch. `chore`, `ci`, `test` and `release` commits and
  merge commits do not release. Below 1.0.0 each level shifts down one.
- **Release names.** The branch is `release/next`, the pull request title is
  `release: <tag>`, and the labels are `release`, `release:rc` and
  `release:major|minor|patch`.
- **Changelog format.** Keep a Changelog sections, grouped by scope.
- **Version sources.** Tags, the archive file, sdist metadata, or a pin.
````

## File: docs/guides/github-workflows.md

````markdown
# GitHub Workflows Guide

Three small jobs cover the whole release flow. Every job that reads a version
needs full history:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
```

Without it, gitversioned exits with code 3 in CI instead of publishing a wrong
version.

## Check pull request titles

```yaml
name: pr-title
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  title:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pipx run gitversioned check "$TITLE"
        env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
```

With squash merges the pull request title becomes the commit subject, so this
one check keeps the history releasable.

## Keep the release pull request up to date

```yaml
name: release-pr
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  release-pr:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned release --pr || [ $? -eq 1 ]
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Exit code 1 means there is nothing to release yet, which is not a failure here.
Add `if: ${{ !startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release') }}` to the
job so the push of a merged release is left to the tagging workflow.
Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not start other
workflows; use a GitHub App token or a personal access token if your checks must
run on the release pull request.

## Tag the merged release and publish

```yaml
name: release
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: write
jobs:
  tag:
    if: startsWith(github.event.head_commit.message, 'release')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned release --tag
      - run: pipx run build
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
```

`release --tag` reads the tag from the merged release commit, refuses a tag that
is not newer than the last release, and pushes it.

## Development and nightly builds

```yaml
- run: echo "VERSION=$(pipx run gitversioned version --type nightly)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
- run: pipx run build
  env:
    GITVERSIONED__TYPE: nightly
```

`--type dev` is the default away from a tag. `--type nightly` has no commit hash
and can be uploaded to a package index. The build plugins take no flags, so the
build reads the type from `GITVERSIONED__TYPE`. For a backend without a plugin,
such as uv_build or Cargo, write it into the files first with
`gitversioned version --write --type nightly`.

## Release without a pull request

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: false
        default: ""
jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: |
          pipx run gitversioned release $VERSION --write
          git add -A
          git commit -qm "release: v$(pipx run gitversioned release $VERSION --json | jq -r .version)"
          git push -q
          pipx run gitversioned release --tag
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
```

An empty input releases the version the commits call for.

## Reject bad tags

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: pipx run gitversioned check --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
```

## Run them

The [github-actions example](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/github-actions)
holds all six workflows and runs every gitversioned step in them on each test
run.
````

## File: docs/guides/hatchling.md

````markdown
# Hatchling Guide

gitversioned plugs into Hatchling as a version source and a build hook. The
version comes from git at build time and nothing is committed.

## Setup

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "my-package"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "gitversioned"

[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]
```

| Piece                                   | What it does                                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gitversioned` in `requires`            | Makes the plugin available to the isolated build.                 |
| `dynamic = ["version"]`                 | Tells the build the version is not in the file.                   |
| `[tool.hatch.version] source`           | Resolves the version from git.                                    |
| `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]` | Writes `<package>/version.py` and adds it to the wheel and sdist. |

`gitversioned init` adds the `[tool.hatch.version]` table for you.

## Read the version at runtime

Add the generated file to `.gitignore`, then import from it:

```gitignore
src/my_package/version.py
```

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
# src/my_package/__init__.py
from my_package.version import __version__
```

The generated module holds `__version__`, `__version_semver__`,
`__version_tuple__`, `__tag__`, `__distance__`, `__commit__` and
`__commit_date__`. It has no build timestamp, so two builds of one commit are
identical.

## Build

```console
$ git tag v1.2.3
$ python -m build
Successfully built my_package-1.2.3.tar.gz and my_package-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl
```

After the tag the same command builds `1.2.4.dev20261125+abc1234`. A wheel built
from the unpacked sdist keeps the sdist's version, because the version is read
from `PKG-INFO` when there is no git history.

## Publishing development builds

Package indexes reject versions with a local part (`+abc1234`). Build a nightly,
which has none, or turn the hash off:

```bash
GITVERSIONED__TYPE=nightly python -m build
GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false python -m build
```

## Settings

Settings go under `[tool.gitversioned]`, never under the Hatch tables. See the
[Configuration Guide](configuration.md). A runnable project is in
[`examples/hatchling`](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/hatchling).
````

## File: docs/guides/maturin.md

````markdown
# Maturin Guide

Maturin takes the version of a Rust extension from `Cargo.toml`. gitversioned
wraps Maturin's build backend: it stamps the resolved version into `Cargo.toml`
for the length of the build, hands over to Maturin, then restores the file.

## Setup

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.0,<2.0", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin"

[project]
name = "my-extension"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.maturin]
python-source = "python"
module-name = "my_extension._native"
```

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "my-extension"
version = "0.0.0"        # a placeholder; never edited by hand
```

Everything under `[tool.maturin]` is passed through untouched. To ship the
generated `version.py` in a mixed Rust and Python project, list it, because
Maturin leaves out files that git ignores:

```toml
[tool.maturin]
include = [{ path = "python/my_extension/version.py", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] }]
```

## Build

```console
$ git tag v0.3.0
$ python -m build --wheel
$ git status --short
```

The wheel is `my_extension-0.3.0-...whl` and the working tree is clean
afterwards. Release candidates are spelled for each side: a tag `v0.3.0-rc.1`
gives the wheel version `0.3.0rc1` and the crate version `0.3.0-rc.1`.

## Cargo on its own

For `cargo build`, `cargo publish` or `maturin develop` outside a PEP 517
build, stamp the manifests first:

```bash
gitversioned version --write
cargo build --release
```

In a workspace this also updates the version of every path dependency on a
workspace crate (the operator, such as `=` or `^`, is kept) and the matching
`Cargo.lock` entries, so `cargo build --locked` keeps working. The stamped
files do not make the tree count as dirty.

A runnable project is in
[`examples/maturin`](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/maturin).
````

## File: docs/guides/migration.md

````markdown
# Migrating from 0.3

Version 0.4 is a rewrite with no compatibility layer. The tool now covers
Python, Rust and npm manifests, checks Conventional Commits and drives
releases, and its surface is much smaller.

## Commands

| 0.3                                             | 0.4                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gitversioned calculate`                        | `gitversioned version`                                  |
| `gitversioned calculate --version-type nightly` | `gitversioned version --type nightly`                   |
| `gitversioned write`                            | `gitversioned version --write`                          |
| `gitversioned format`                           | `gitversioned version --write --dry-run`                |
| `gitversioned overrides`                        | `gitversioned version --write` (targets are discovered) |
| `gitversioned init-archive`                     | `gitversioned init`                                     |
| No equivalent                                   | `gitversioned check`, `gitversioned release`            |

## Settings

Old keys are rejected with an error that names the nearest new key.

| 0.3                                                      | 0.4                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `output`, `output_strategies`                            | Removed. `version.py` is generated in one fixed shape.            |
| `overrides`                                              | `[[targets]]` with `key` or `pattern`; most files are discovered. |
| `version_type`                                           | `--type` on the command line.                                     |
| `version_standard`                                       | `--standard`; each file gets its own spelling.                    |
| `regex_tag` and the other `regex_*` keys                 | `tag = "v{version}"`.                                             |
| `format_main`, `format_dev`, `format_pre`, `format_post` | Fixed shapes; choose the base with `dev` and `nightly`.           |
| `auto_increment`                                         | `dev` and `nightly`.                                              |
| `source_type`, `version_source_*`                        | Removed. Sources are tried in a fixed order.                      |
| `dirty_ignore`                                           | Removed. Stamped files never count as dirty.                      |

Environment overrides are spelled `GITVERSIONED__KEY`, with two underscores.

## Build backends

| Backend    | Change                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hatchling  | Keep `source = "gitversioned"`. Add `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]` for `version.py`. |
| Setuptools | Now opt-in: list `gitversioned` in `build-system.requires`.                                   |
| Maturin    | Set `build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin"`.                                         |

## Version shapes

Development versions changed from a commit count to the commit date:
`1.2.1.dev4+gabc1234` is now `1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234`. Nightly versions have
no local part. Tags are read the same way, so existing tags keep working.

## Python API

`Settings`, the strategy classes and the template helpers are gone. Use
`load_config`, `resolve`, `stamp` and `plan_release`; see the
[API Guide](api.md).
````

## File: docs/guides/setuptools.md

````markdown
# Setuptools Guide

The setuptools integration is opt-in, so installing gitversioned next to an
unrelated setuptools project never changes that project's version.

## Setup

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=64", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "my-package"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
```

Listing `gitversioned` in `build-system.requires` is the opt-in. A project that
still uses `setup.py` can opt in with a keyword instead:

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
# setup.py
from setuptools import setup

setup(gitversioned=True)
```

## What the build does

The build resolves the version from git, sets it as the distribution's version
and writes `<package>/version.py` so the installed package can report it. Add
that file to `.gitignore`:

```gitignore
src/my_package/version.py
```

<!--phmdoctest-skip-->

```python
# src/my_package/__init__.py
from my_package.version import __version__
```

```console
$ git tag v2.1.0
$ python -m build --wheel
Successfully built my_package-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

## Settings

Settings can live in `[tool.gitversioned]` in `pyproject.toml` or in
`[tool:gitversioned]` in `setup.cfg`:

```ini
# setup.cfg
[tool:gitversioned]
fallback = 0.1.0
scopes = ["core", "docs"]
```

See the [Configuration Guide](configuration.md). A runnable project is in
[`examples/setuptools`](https://github.com/markurtz/git-versioned/tree/main/examples/setuptools).

## Coming from setuptools-scm

- Tags are read the same way, so existing `v1.2.3` tags keep working.
- An existing `.git_archival.txt` is read as it is.
- `write_to` / `version_file` is replaced by the generated `version.py`.
- Remove `setuptools-scm` from `build-system.requires` and delete
  `[tool.setuptools_scm]`.
````

## File: examples/ci-safety/README.md

````markdown
# No silent wrong versions in CI

A wrong version that nobody notices is worse than a failed build. When
gitversioned cannot trust what it sees (a shallow clone, a folder with no git
history) it warns on a developer machine and fails in CI, where the `CI`
variable is set. `gitversioned init` adds the archive file that lets a source
tarball keep its version.

| Level        | Shows                                                     | Needs |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | `check`, `init`, `CI`, `.git_archival.txt`, `GITVERSIONED__VERSION` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

### Set up the project

`init` adds `.git_archival.txt` and its `export-subst` line in
`.gitattributes`, and points Hatchling at gitversioned. It says what is left to
do by hand, if anything:

```console
$ git init -q && gitversioned init
wrote  .git_archival.txt
edit   .gitattributes          + .git_archival.txt  export-subst
edit   pyproject.toml          + [tool.hatch.version] source = "gitversioned"
edit   pyproject.toml          + [tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]
No gitversioned settings needed: defaults and discovery cover this repo.
$ cat .gitattributes
.git_archival.txt  export-subst
$ cat .git_archival.txt
node: $Format:%H$
node-date: $Format:%cI$
describe-name: $Format:%(describe:tags=true,match=*[0-9]*)$
ref-names: $Format:%D$
$ grep -A1 "tool.hatch.version" pyproject.toml
[tool.hatch.version]
source = "gitversioned"
```

`init` is optional: a repository rendered from markurtz/template already has
these files.

```console
$ git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.3.0
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix: second" && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix: third"
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v1.3.0
ok    targets       src/safety/version.py
ok    archive file  .git_archival.txt and .gitattributes export-subst
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

### A shallow clone

`actions/checkout` fetches one commit by default, so no tag is in reach. On a
laptop that is a warning; in CI it is an error with exit code 3 that says how
to fix it:

```console
$ git clone -q --depth 1 "file://$PWD" ../shallow
$ gitversioned version -C ../shallow
WARNING shallow clone with no release tags reachable, so the version cannot be trusted. Fetch full history (fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout).
0.1.0.dev20261125+4fb137b
$ CI=true gitversioned version -C ../shallow
fail  shallow clone with no release tags reachable, so the version cannot be trusted. Fetch full history (fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout).
[exit 3]
$ CI=true gitversioned check -C ../shallow | grep git
fail  git           shallow clone, no tags reachable. Set fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout.
ok    archive file  .git_archival.txt and .gitattributes export-subst
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
[exit 3]
```

With the full history (`fetch-depth: 0`) the version is right again:

```console
$ cd ../shallow && git fetch -q --unshallow --tags && CI=true gitversioned version
1.3.1.dev20261125+4fb137b
```

### A source tarball

`git archive` fills in `.git_archival.txt`, so a tarball downloaded from a tag
or a commit keeps its version with no `.git` folder at all:

```console
$ mkdir ../at-tag && git archive v1.3.0 | tar -x -C ../at-tag
$ CI=true gitversioned version -C ../at-tag
1.3.0
$ mkdir ../at-main && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C ../at-main
$ CI=true gitversioned version -C ../at-main --explain
version   1.3.1.dev20261125+4fb137b
type      dev
current   1.3.0  (tag v1.3.0, 4fb137b, 2 commits since)
note      base 1.3.0 from .git_archival.txt (v1.3.0)
config    defaults  (0 keys set, 14 defaults)
```

A copy without the archive file has nothing to go on, so CI stops:

```console
$ mkdir ../copy && cp -r src pyproject.toml ../copy
$ CI=true gitversioned version -C ../copy
fail  no git repository, archive file or package metadata found, so the version cannot be resolved; using fallback 0.1.0. Set GITVERSIONED__VERSION to pin one.
[exit 3]
```

A build job that already knows the version pins it, as
`SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION` does for setuptools-scm:

```console
$ CI=true GITVERSIONED__VERSION=1.3.0 gitversioned version -C ../copy
1.3.0
```

### A brand-new repository

A full clone with no release tag yet is not a problem to report: the history
proves there is no tag, so CI builds the fallback version.

```console
$ git init -q ../fresh && cd ../fresh && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: start"
$ cd ../fresh && CI=true gitversioned version
0.1.0-dev.20261125+8fd1f5c
```

## How it works

- Sources are read in a fixed order: a pin, git tags, the archive file, an
  sdist's `PKG-INFO`, then the fallback.
- `CI` is the switch between warning and failing. GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and
  most other systems set it.

## Next

- [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) for `fetch-depth: 0` in a workflow.
- [hatchling](../hatchling/README.md) for the sdist path.
````

## File: examples/commit-checks/README.md

````markdown
# Pull request titles and commit messages

`gitversioned check` validates Conventional Commit subjects the same way in a
pull request workflow, in a commit-msg hook and in a terminal, against one list
of types and one list of scopes.

| Level    | Shows                                                         | Needs |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Beginner | `check TITLE`, `--commits`, `--file`, `--warn`, `--tag`, `--json`, `scopes` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

### Titles

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "chore: start" && git tag v1.0.0
$ gitversioned check "feat(cli): add --explain"
ok
$ gitversioned check "fix!: drop Python 3.9"
ok
$ gitversioned check "added explain"
fail  title  'added explain' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate, release.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned check "feat(gui): add a window"
fail  title  unknown scope 'gui'. Scopes: core, cli, docs, deps, ci, release.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned check "wip: half done"
fail  title  unknown type 'wip'. Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate, release.
[exit 1]
```

The default types are the template's twelve: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`,
`refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`, `deprecate` and
`release`. Scopes are open unless `scopes` lists them, as
[`gitversioned.toml`](gitversioned.toml) does here.

`--json` gives the same answer to a script:

```console
$ gitversioned check "feat(gui): add a window" --json
{
  "ok": false,
  "findings": [
    {
      "status": "fail",
      "area": "title",
      "message": "unknown scope 'gui'. Scopes: core, cli, docs, deps, ci, release."
    }
  ]
}
[exit 1]
```

### Every commit on a branch

`--commits` takes any git range, so a pull request can check each commit, not
only its title:

```console
$ git switch -q -c topic
$ echo a >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "feat(core): parse the input"
$ echo b >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "updated stuff"
$ gitversioned check --commits main..HEAD
fail  5580f3f  'updated stuff' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate, release.
[exit 1]
$ git reset -q --hard HEAD~1 && gitversioned check --commits main..HEAD
ok    commits  1 commit
```

### A commit-msg hook that only warns

`--file` reads the message git is about to commit, and `--warn` reports a
problem without blocking the commit:

```console
$ printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec gitversioned check --file "$1" --warn\n' > .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
$ echo c >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "tweak things"
warn  title  'tweak things' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate, release.
$ git log -1 --format=%s
tweak things
$ echo d >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "docs: explain the hook"
ok
```

Git's own subjects (merges, `fixup!` and `squash!`) are not checked.

```console
$ echo e >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "fixup! docs: explain the hook"
ok
```

### Tags

`--tag` checks a tag name before a release: it must match the tag template and
be newer than the last release.

```console
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.1.0
ok    tag  1.1.0, newer than v1.0.0
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.1.0-rc.1
ok    tag  1.1.0rc1, newer than v1.0.0
$ gitversioned check --tag v0.9.0
fail  tag  0.9.0 is not newer than v1.0.0.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned check --tag release-1.1
fail  tag  'release-1.1' is not a release tag. Expected vX.Y.Z with an optional pre-release such as -rc.1.
[exit 1]
```

## How it works

- [`gitversioned.toml`](gitversioned.toml) sets `scopes`. `types` replaces the
  default type list the same way. `scopes` can also name a TOML file whose
  tables are the scopes, as the [template-polyglot](../template-polyglot/README.md)
  example does with `.config/blocks.toml`.
- Exit codes: 0 when everything passes, 1 when a check fails, 2 for bad usage.

## Next

- [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) for the pull request title job.
- [next-version](../next-version/README.md) for what each type does to the version.
````

## File: examples/configuration/README.md

````markdown
# Settings, homes and the environment

A repository needs no settings at all. When it does have some, they live in
exactly one of six homes, unknown keys are errors that name the nearest valid
one, and every root key can come from the environment instead.

| Level        | Shows                                                               | Needs |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | the six homes, `GITVERSIONED__KEY`, `tag`, `fallback`, `-v`, `-q`, exit code 2 | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

### Defaults

`--explain` names where the settings came from:

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.0.0
$ gitversioned version --explain | tail -1
config    defaults  (0 keys set, 14 defaults)
```

### One home

The first home found wins: `.config/gitversioned.toml`, `gitversioned.toml`,
`[tool.gitversioned]` in `pyproject.toml`, `[workspace.metadata.gitversioned]`
in `Cargo.toml`, `"gitversioned"` in `package.json`, then
`[tool:gitversioned]` in `setup.cfg`.

```console
$ printf 'annotated = true\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version --explain | tail -1
config    gitversioned.toml  (1 key set, 13 defaults)
$ printf '{"name": "demo", "version": "0.0.0", "gitversioned": {"branch": "trunk"}}\n' > package.json
$ gitversioned version
fail  settings found in two homes: gitversioned.toml and package.json "gitversioned". Keep them in one file.
[exit 2]
$ rm gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version --explain | tail -1
config    package.json "gitversioned"  (1 key set, 13 defaults)
$ rm package.json
```

### Mistakes are errors

An unknown key names the nearest valid one, and so does a 0.3 key that no
longer exists. Bad configuration exits with code 2:

```console
$ printf 'tga = "v{version}"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version
fail  unknown key `tga` in gitversioned.toml. Did you mean `tag`? Valid keys: version, fallback, tag, annotated, branch, dev, nightly, date, local, changelog, types, scopes, targets, packages.
[exit 2]
$ printf 'version_type = "dev"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version
fail  unknown key `version_type` in gitversioned.toml. `version_type` was removed in 0.4: pass --type on the command line. Valid keys: version, fallback, tag, annotated, branch, dev, nightly, date, local, changelog, types, scopes, targets, packages.
[exit 2]
$ printf 'dev = "huge"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version
fail  invalid config in gitversioned.toml: dev: Input should be 'patch', 'minor', 'major' or 'next'
[exit 2]
$ rm gitversioned.toml
```

### Tag names

`tag` is both how release tags are named and how they are recognised. A
repository that tags `release-2.1.0` says so once:

```console
$ git tag release-2.1.0 && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix: after the release"
$ printf 'tag = "release-{version}"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version --explain | sed -n '1,3p'
version   2.1.1-dev.20261125+2914331
type      dev
current   2.1.0  (tag release-2.1.0, 2914331, 1 commit since)
$ gitversioned check --tag release-2.2.0
ok    tag  2.2.0, newer than release-2.1.0
$ rm gitversioned.toml
```

### The environment

Any root key can be set as `GITVERSIONED__KEY`, which wins over the file. A
build job pins the version once and passes it on with `GITVERSIONED__VERSION`:

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__TAG='release-{version}' gitversioned version
2.1.1-dev.20261125+2914331
$ GITVERSIONED__VERSION=9.9.9 gitversioned version --explain
version   9.9.9
type      release
current   none (version given by the pin)
note      pinned to 9.9.9
config    defaults  (1 key set, 13 defaults)
```

A misspelled variable is not silently ignored:

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__TAGG='release-{version}' gitversioned version
WARNING ignoring unknown environment override GITVERSIONED__TAGG. Did you mean `tag`?
1.0.1-dev.20261125+2914331
```

`fallback` is the base before the first matching tag:

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__TAG='pkg-v{version}' GITVERSIONED__FALLBACK=0.0.1 gitversioned version
WARNING tags release-2.1.0, v1.0.0 look like versions but do not match the tag template 'pkg-v{version}'; using fallback 0.0.1. Set `tag` to match them.
0.0.1-dev.20261125+2914331
```

### How much it says

Results go to stdout and everything else to stderr. `-v` adds detail, `-vv`
debug output, and `-q` keeps only errors:

```console
$ gitversioned version -v
INFO    settings from defaults: all defaults
INFO    version 1.0.1.dev20261125+2914331 (dev, from tag); tag v1.0.0, 1 commit since
1.0.1-dev.20261125+2914331
$ GITVERSIONED__TAG='pkg-v{version}' gitversioned version -q
0.1.0-dev.20261125+2914331
```

## How it works

- The [configuration guide](https://markurtz.github.io/git-versioned/guides/configuration/)
  lists every key and its default.
- Two homes with settings in them are an error that names both files, so the
  answer never depends on which file was read first.

## Next

- [custom-targets](../custom-targets/README.md) for `[[targets]]`.
- [monorepo-packages](../monorepo-packages/README.md) for `[packages]`.
````

## File: examples/custom-targets/README.md

````markdown
# Files discovery cannot find

Discovery finds the standard manifests by name. Everything else is listed once
in `[[targets]]`: a dotted `key` for TOML, JSON and YAML files, or a regular
expression `pattern` for any other text file. This covers release-please's
`extra-files`, cargo-release's `pre-release-replacements` and bump-my-version's
search and replace.

| Level        | Shows                                                       | Needs |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | `[[targets]]` `path`, `key`, `pattern`, `commit`; `release --write` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.1.0
$ gitversioned check | sed -n '3p'
ok    targets       api/openapi.yaml, web/manifest.json, deploy.toml, go/version/version.go, INSTALL.md, install.sh, lib/_version.py
$ gitversioned version --write
1.1.0
  api/openapi.yaml       1.1.0
  web/manifest.json      1.1.0
  deploy.toml            1.1.0
  go/version/version.go  1.1.0
  INSTALL.md             1.1.0
  install.sh             1.1.0
  lib/_version.py        1.1.0
$ git diff -U0 | grep '^[-+][^-+]'
-pip install relay==1.0.0
+pip install relay==1.1.0
-  version: 0.0.0
+  version: 1.1.0
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "1.1.0"
-const Version = "0.0.0"
+const Version = "1.1.0"
-VERSION="0.0.0" # x-version
+VERSION="1.1.0" # x-version
-__version__ = "0.0.0"
+__version__ = "1.1.0"
-  "version": "0.0.0"
+  "version": "1.1.0"
```

Each value is the only thing that changed, and each file is spelled for its
ecosystem: SemVer everywhere except the `.py` file, which gets PEP 440. A
release candidate shows the difference:

```console
$ git checkout -q . && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: next" && git tag v1.2.0-rc.1
$ gitversioned version --write >/dev/null
$ grep -h -E 'Version =|__version__|version:' go/version/version.go lib/_version.py api/openapi.yaml
const Version = "1.2.0-rc.1"
__version__ = "1.2.0rc1"
  version: 1.2.0-rc.1
```

### Released files and built files

A release commits every target except those with `commit = false`, so the
repository keeps the placeholder in `lib/_version.py` while builds stamp it:

```console
$ git checkout -q . && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix: final touches"
$ gitversioned release 1.2.0 --write
release   1.2.0  (set by VERSION, from 1.2.0rc1)
tag       v1.2.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, api/openapi.yaml, web/manifest.json, deploy.toml, go/version/version.go, INSTALL.md, install.sh

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- next

### Fixed

- final touches

Wrote CHANGELOG.md, api/openapi.yaml, web/manifest.json, deploy.toml, go/version/version.go, INSTALL.md, install.sh.
$ git status --short
 M INSTALL.md
 M api/openapi.yaml
 M deploy.toml
 M go/version/version.go
 M install.sh
 M web/manifest.json
?? CHANGELOG.md
```

### Mistakes are reported

A pattern without a `version` group, or a key on a file type that has no keys,
is a configuration error:

```console
$ printf '[[targets]]\npath = "install.sh"\npattern = "VERSION=.*"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version --write
fail  target install.sh: pattern needs a (?P<version>...) group
[exit 2]
$ printf '[[targets]]\npath = "install.sh"\nkey = "version"\n' > gitversioned.toml && gitversioned version --write
fail  target install.sh: `key` works for .toml, .json, .yaml and .yml files. Use `pattern` for other files.
[exit 2]
```

## How it works

- [`gitversioned.toml`](gitversioned.toml) lists seven targets. The file name
  decides the spelling: PEP 440 for `.py` files and `pyproject.toml`, SemVer
  for the rest.
- `key` is a dotted path from the top of the document. `pattern` is a Python
  regular expression in multi-line mode; every match is replaced.
- Listed targets add to discovery. Listing a discovered file replaces its
  default handling, for example to point a `key` at another field.

## Next

- [polyglot](../polyglot/README.md) for discovered and listed targets together.
- [release-local](../release-local/README.md) for the release that commits them.
````

## File: examples/docker/README.md

````markdown
# Container images

Container images take the version three ways: an OCI version label written into
the Dockerfile, a build argument, and the image tags. Registries refuse `+` in a
tag, so an image of a development build uses a nightly version or turns the
local part off.

| Level        | Shows                                                                       | Needs |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | `Dockerfile` and `Containerfile` labels, `--standard semver`, `--json`, `--type nightly` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v2.3.0
$ gitversioned version --write
2.3.0
  Dockerfile  2.3.0
$ git diff -U0 | grep '^[-+][^-+]'
-      org.opencontainers.image.version="0.0.0"
+      org.opencontainers.image.version="2.3.0"
```

The label in `worker/Containerfile` reads a build argument, so it is not a
target. Pass the version as that argument:

```console
$ echo docker build --build-arg VERSION="$(gitversioned version)" -t relay:"$(gitversioned version)" .
docker build --build-arg VERSION=2.3.0 -t relay:2.3.0 .
```

### Tags for a release

A release workflow tags a final release `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y`, `X` and `latest`, and a
pre-release only with its own version, so `latest` stays on the last final
release. `--json` says which one it is:

```console
$ gitversioned version --json | python -c 'import json, sys; v = json.load(sys.stdin); x, y, z = v["semver"].split(".")[:3]; print(" ".join([v["semver"]] if v["prerelease"] else [v["semver"], f"{x}.{y}", x, "latest"]))'
2.3.0 2.3 2 latest
$ git checkout -q . && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: new endpoint" && git tag v2.4.0-rc.1
$ gitversioned version --json | python -c 'import json, sys; v = json.load(sys.stdin); x, y, z = v["semver"].split(".")[:3]; print(" ".join([v["semver"]] if v["prerelease"] else [v["semver"], f"{x}.{y}", x, "latest"]))'
2.4.0-rc.1
```

### Nightly images

A development version carries `+<hash>`, which is not a valid image tag. A
nightly image uses `--type nightly`, which never has a local part, or turns the
local part off with `GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false`:

```console
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix: nightly fix"
$ gitversioned version
2.4.0-rc.2.dev.20261125+f2c7d19
$ gitversioned version --type nightly
2.4.0-rc.2.nightly.20261125
$ GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false gitversioned version
2.4.0-rc.2.dev.20261125
```

## How it works

- The OCI label `org.opencontainers.image.version` is discovered in any
  `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.<name>`, `<name>.Dockerfile` or `Containerfile`,
  unless its value is a `$` reference.
- Docker is not needed to run this example; the `docker build` line is printed,
  not run.

## Next

- [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) for the nightly workflow.
- [polyglot](../polyglot/README.md) for a Dockerfile next to other manifests.
````

## File: examples/github-actions/README.md

````markdown
# GitHub Actions workflows

Six workflows cover the whole release flow: pull request titles, the release
pull request, tagging and publishing the merge, a manual release, nightly
builds and hand-pushed tags. They sit in [`.github/workflows/`](.github/workflows)
ready to copy, and every step that runs gitversioned is run below.

| Level    | Shows                                                       | Needs                         |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| Advanced | `check`, `release --pr`, `release --tag`, nightly builds, CI safety | git, Python, `build`, `gh` signed in |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. A bare repository
stands in for GitHub and a stand-in `gh` keeps pull requests in a JSON file.
[`ci.py`](ci.py) runs a workflow's steps the way a runner would: each `run` step
in `bash` with its `env` and `CI=true`, `${{ … }}` filled from `--event`, and
`uses` steps skipped because this folder is already the checkout.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first release" && git tag v1.0.0
$ git init -q --bare ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git && git push -q -u origin main v1.0.0
```

### Pull request titles

[`pr-title.yml`](.github/workflows/pr-title.yml) checks the title, which a
squash merge turns into the commit subject:

```console
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/pr-title.yml --event github.event.pull_request.title="feat(cli): add --explain"
job title
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Check the title
ok
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/pr-title.yml --event github.event.pull_request.title="Add explain flag"
job title
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Check the title
fail  title  'Add explain flag' is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected type(scope): subject. Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert, deprecate, release.
  failed with exit code 1
[exit 1]
```

### The release pull request

The pull request merges, and the push to `main` starts both
[`release-pr.yml`](.github/workflows/release-pr.yml) and
[`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml). Only the first runs, since the
commit is not a release:

```console
$ echo "a = 1" > src/beam/a.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(cli): add --explain (#12)" && git push -q
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/release-pr.yml --event github.event.head_commit.message="feat(cli): add --explain (#12)"
job release-pr
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Open or update the release pull request
release   1.1.0
branch    release/next  (rebuilt from main)
commit    release: v1.1.0
pr        #57 opened  https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/57
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/release.yml --event github.event.head_commit.message="feat(cli): add --explain (#12)"
job tag: skipped
```

Merging the release pull request is the release. On that push only
`release.yml` runs: it tags the merge, pushes the tag, and builds from it:

```console
$ git merge -q --squash origin/release/next >/dev/null && git commit -qm "release: v1.1.0 (#57)" && git push -q && gh pr merge 57 --squash
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/release-pr.yml --event github.event.head_commit.message="release: v1.1.0 (#57)"
job release-pr: skipped
$ python ci.py .github/workflows/release.yml --event github.event.head_commit.message="release: v1.1.0 (#57)"
job tag
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Tag the release commit
tag       v1.1.0 at 4fd52b0, pushed
  step Build
beam-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
beam-1.1.0.tar.gz
  uses pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1: skipped
$ git ls-remote --tags origin | sed 's/^[0-9a-f]*\t//'
refs/tags/v1.0.0
refs/tags/v1.1.0
```

### Hand-pushed tags

[`tag-check.yml`](.github/workflows/tag-check.yml) runs on every pushed tag. A
tag pushed by hand that is not newer than the last release fails:

```console
$ GITHUB_REF_NAME=v1.1.0 python ci.py .github/workflows/tag-check.yml
job check
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Check the tag
ok    tag        1.1.0 at HEAD, newer than v1.0.0
ok    changelog  CHANGELOG.md has the section
$ git tag v1.0.1 && GITHUB_REF_NAME=v1.0.1 python ci.py .github/workflows/tag-check.yml
job check
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Check the tag
fail  tag  1.0.1 is not newer than v1.1.0.
  failed with exit code 1
[exit 1]
$ git tag -d v1.0.1 >/dev/null
```

### Nightly builds

[`nightly.yml`](.github/workflows/nightly.yml) builds the next release as a
dated nightly, with no commit hash, so a package index accepts it. The build
plugin reads the type from `GITVERSIONED__TYPE`, and nothing is committed:

```console
$ echo "b = 1" > src/beam/b.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): handle empty input (#14)" && git push -q
$ rm -rf dist && python ci.py .github/workflows/nightly.yml
job nightly
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Version
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 2 release tags, latest v1.1.0
ok    targets       src/beam/version.py
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
ok    github        gh is signed in
  env VERSION=1.1.1.dev20261125
  step Build
beam-1.1.1.dev20261125-py3-none-any.whl
beam-1.1.1.dev20261125.tar.gz
$ git status --short
```

### Full history is required

Every job that reads a version checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`. In a shallow
clone gitversioned stops with exit code 3 in CI instead of building a wrong
version:

```console
$ git clone -q --depth 1 file://$PWD/../origin.git ../shallow && cd ../shallow && CI=true gitversioned version
fail  shallow clone with no release tags reachable, so the version cannot be trusted. Fetch full history (fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout).
[exit 3]
```

### A manual release

[`release-manual.yml`](.github/workflows/release-manual.yml) releases without
the pull request, at the version given or the next one:

```console
$ rm -rf dist && python ci.py .github/workflows/release-manual.yml --event inputs.version=2.0.0
job release
  uses actions/checkout@v4: skipped
  step Write the release
release   2.0.0  (set by VERSION, from 1.1.0)
tag       v2.0.0
files     CHANGELOG.md

## [2.0.0] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed
````
