- **core**: handle empty input (#14)

Wrote CHANGELOG.md.
  step Tag it
tag       v2.0.0 at 0f9c04b, pushed
$ git log --oneline -1 origin/main && git ls-remote --tags origin v2.0.0 | sed 's/^[0-9a-f]*\t//'
0f9c04b release: v2.0.0
refs/tags/v2.0.0
```

## How it works

- Every workflow pins its permissions: `contents: write` to push tags and the
  release branch, `pull-requests: write` for the release pull request, and
  `id-token: write` for trusted publishing to PyPI.
- `release-pr.yml` accepts exit code 1, which means nothing is releasable yet.
  It skips release commits, which `release.yml` handles.
- Pull requests opened with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` start no other
  workflows. Use a GitHub App token if checks must run on the release pull
  request.
- `release --tag` refuses a tag that is not newer than the last release, so a
  rerun of `release.yml` cannot tag twice.
- The [GitHub Workflows guide](https://markurtz.github.io/git-versioned/guides/github-workflows/)
  explains each workflow.

## Next

- [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md) for the release pull request in detail,
  with candidates and labels.
- [ci-safety](../ci-safety/README.md) for every check that stops a CI build.
````

## File: examples/hatchling/README.md

````markdown
# Hatchling, zero config

A pure Python package built with Hatchling whose version comes from its git
tags. Nothing is configured: there is no `[tool.gitversioned]` table.

| Level    | Build backend | Needs                     |
| -------- | ------------- | ------------------------- |
| Beginner | Hatchling     | Python, `build`, `hatchling` |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version"
$ git tag v1.2.3
$ gitversioned version
1.2.3
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v1.2.3
ok    targets       src/demo_hatch/version.py
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

Build a wheel and an sdist. Both are named for the tag, and the wheel carries a
generated `version.py`:

```console
$ python -m build --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_hatch-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl
demo_hatch-1.2.3.tar.gz
$ unzip -p dist/demo_hatch-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl demo_hatch/version.py | grep -E "^__(version|tag|distance)__"
__version__ = version = "1.2.3"
__tag__ = "v1.2.3"
__distance__ = 0
$ git status --short
```

A commit after the tag gives a development version, one patch above the tag,
dated by the commit and carrying the commit hash as a local part:

```console
$ echo '"""A demo package."""' > src/demo_hatch/extra.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix: add a module"
$ gitversioned version
1.2.4.dev20261125+488b5b3
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.2.4-dev.20261125+488b5b3
```

The sdist builds again without git, from the version recorded in its
`PKG-INFO`, which is how pip installs it:

```console
$ mkdir ../unpacked && tar -xzf dist/demo_hatch-1.2.3.tar.gz -C ../unpacked
$ cd ../unpacked/demo_hatch-1.2.3 && python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_hatch-1.2.3-py3-none-any.whl
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) has three gitversioned lines:
  `gitversioned` in `build-system.requires`, `source = "gitversioned"` under
  `[tool.hatch.version]`, and the `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]` table,
  which writes `src/demo_hatch/version.py` into the wheel and the sdist.
- [`.gitignore`](.gitignore) ignores `version.py`, so it is never committed and
  builds never make the tree dirty.
- [`src/demo_hatch/__init__.py`](src/demo_hatch/__init__.py) re-exports
  `__version__` from the generated module.

## Next

- [setuptools](../setuptools/README.md) for the same with setuptools.
- [version-shapes](../version-shapes/README.md) for every version gitversioned prints.
````

## File: examples/maturin/README.md

````markdown
# Maturin through the wrapper backend

A Rust extension for Python, built by Maturin. Maturin reads the version from
`Cargo.toml`, which stays at the placeholder `0.0.0` in git. The
`gitversioned.plugins.maturin` backend stamps the resolved version into
`Cargo.toml` for the length of the build, hands over to Maturin, and puts the
file back, so the tree stays clean.

| Level        | Build backend                     | Needs                                    |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Intermediate | `gitversioned.plugins.maturin`    | Python, `build`, `maturin`, a Rust toolchain |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates. The first build compiles PyO3 and takes a minute.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v0.3.0
$ python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_maturin-0.3.0-...whl
$ git status --short
$ grep '^version' Cargo.toml
version = "0.0.0"
```

The extension reports the version Cargo compiled into it, and the Python
package the one in its generated `version.py`; both are the tag's:

```console
$ unzip -q dist/*.whl -d ../site
$ PYTHONPATH=../site python -c "import demo_maturin, demo_maturin.version as v; print(demo_maturin.__version__, v.__version__, demo_maturin.add(2, 3))"
0.3.0 0.3.0 5
```

A release candidate tag is spelled for each ecosystem: SemVer in `Cargo.toml`,
PEP 440 in the wheel name.

```console
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: add more" && git tag v0.4.0-rc.1
$ gitversioned version --write --dry-run | sed -n '1,8p'
0.4.0rc1
--- a/Cargo.toml
+++ b/Cargo.toml
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 [package]
 name = "demo-maturin"
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.4.0-rc.1"
$ rm -rf dist && python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_maturin-0.4.0rc1-...whl
```

`gitversioned version --write` stamps `Cargo.toml` for a plain `cargo build`
too. The edit does not make the tree dirty, so the version stays clean:

```console
$ gitversioned version --write >/dev/null && git status --short && gitversioned version
 M Cargo.toml
0.4.0rc1
$ git checkout -q Cargo.toml
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) sets
  `build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin"` and lists both `maturin` and
  `gitversioned` in `build-system.requires`.
- [`Cargo.toml`](Cargo.toml) keeps `version = "0.0.0"` in git.
- [`src/lib.rs`](src/lib.rs) exposes `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` as `__version__`.
- The [template-polyglot](../template-polyglot/README.md) example shows the
  other way: the plain `maturin` backend reading a workspace version that
  `version --write` stamped.

## Next

- [rust-workspace](../rust-workspace/README.md) for a Cargo workspace without Python.
````

## File: examples/monorepo-packages/README.md

````markdown
# Packages with their own tags

A repository with a main Python package at the root and two packages under
`packages/`. `packages/core` has its own tags (`core-v0.5.0`) and its own
release line, like a release-please manifest entry or a release-plz crate.
`packages/web` has no tag, so it always ships with the repository's version.

| Level    | Shows                                                         | Needs  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Advanced | `[packages]`, `-p`, package tags, per-package changelogs and builds | Python |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.0.0 && git tag core-v0.5.0
$ gitversioned version
1.0.0
$ gitversioned version -p core
0.5.0
$ gitversioned version -p web
1.0.0
```

### Commits belong to one line

A commit under `packages/core` moves only the core's line. The repository is
still on its release, because the core's folder is not part of it:

```console
$ echo "x = 1" > packages/core/src/mono_core/fast.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): faster parsing"
$ gitversioned version
1.0.0
$ gitversioned version -p core
0.5.1.dev20261125+7a3f4c7
$ gitversioned version -p core --next
0.5.1
$ gitversioned version --next
fail  Nothing to release since 1.0.0: no commit since is a feat, a fix or another releasable type.
[exit 1]
```

A commit under `packages/web` belongs to the repository, since web follows it:

```console
$ echo '<h1>hi</h1>' > packages/web/index.html && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(web): add a page"
$ gitversioned version --next
1.1.0
$ gitversioned version --write | grep web
  packages/web/package.json  1.0.1-dev.20261125+44b8223
$ git checkout -q packages/web
```

### Release the core on its own

`-p core` plans, writes and tags the core's release, with its own changelog in
its folder:

```console
$ gitversioned release -p core
release   0.5.1  (patch, from commits, from 0.5.0)
tag       core-v0.5.1
files     packages/core/CHANGELOG.md

## [0.5.1] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed

- **core**: faster parsing

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.
$ gitversioned release -p core --write >/dev/null && git add -A && git commit -qm "release(core): core-v0.5.1"
$ gitversioned release -p core --tag
tag       core-v0.5.1 at 997d17e, created locally
$ git tag --list
core-v0.5.0
core-v0.5.1
v1.0.0
```

A build from the package's folder follows the package's tag:

```console
$ cd packages/core && python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
mono_core-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

Packages without their own tag are released with the repository, and
`check --tag` validates package tags too:

```console
$ gitversioned release -p web
fail  package 'web' has no `tag` of its own, so it is released with the repository. Run the release without -p, or give the package a `tag` such as "web-v{version}".
[exit 2]
$ gitversioned check --tag core-v0.5.1 -p core
ok    tag        0.5.1 at HEAD, newer than core-v0.5.0
ok    changelog  packages/core/CHANGELOG.md has the section
```

## How it works

- [`gitversioned.toml`](gitversioned.toml) lists both packages; only `core` has
  a `tag`.
- Each package's targets, commits and changelog are scoped to its `path`.
  Folders of packages with their own tag are left out of the repository's.
- A build plugin finds the package a build folder belongs to, so
  `packages/core/pyproject.toml` needs no settings of its own.

## Next

- [polyglot](../polyglot/README.md) for a package with its own tag among many manifests.
- [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md) for release pull requests per package.
````

## File: examples/next-version/README.md

````markdown
# The next version and why

How gitversioned picks the next release from Conventional Commits, and every
way to override it. The project is a plain folder with no manifest, so versions
print in SemVer.

| Level        | Shows                                                                 | Needs |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | `version --next`, `--explain`, `--bump`, `--pre`, `GITVERSIONED__BUMP` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

### Levels from commits

A fix asks for a patch release, a feature for a minor one, and a breaking change
(`!` after the type, or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) for a major one. `chore`,
`ci` and `test` ask for nothing.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.2.0
$ echo fix >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "fix(core): handle empty input (#40)"
$ gitversioned version --next
1.2.1
$ echo feat >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "feat(cli): add --explain (#41)"
$ echo chore >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "chore(deps): bump ruff (#42)"
$ gitversioned version --next --explain
next      1.3.0
current   1.2.0  (tag v1.2.0, c3bebe5, 3 commits since)
why       minor, the highest level of 3 commits since v1.2.0
  none    chore(deps): bump ruff (#42)
  minor   feat(cli): add --explain (#41)
  patch   fix(core): handle empty input (#40)
note      base 1.2.0 from tag v1.2.0
config    defaults  (0 keys set, 14 defaults)
```

A breaking change in the footer counts the same as `!`:

```console
$ echo api >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "refactor(core): rename the entry point" -m "BREAKING CHANGE: run() is now main()."
$ gitversioned version --next
2.0.0
```

### Overrides

`--bump` forces a level, and `GITVERSIONED__BUMP` does the same from the
environment, or names the version outright, like release-please's `Release-As`:

```console
$ gitversioned version --next --bump minor
1.3.0
$ GITVERSIONED__BUMP=patch gitversioned version --next
1.2.1
$ GITVERSIONED__BUMP=4.0.0 gitversioned version --next
4.0.0
```

### Pre-releases

`--pre` makes the next version a pre-release and numbers it from the tags that
already exist. `rc`, `beta` and `alpha` work the same way:

```console
$ gitversioned version --next --pre beta
2.0.0-beta.1
$ gitversioned version --next --pre rc
2.0.0-rc.1
$ git tag v2.0.0-rc.1
$ echo more >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "fix(core): late fix"
$ gitversioned version --next --pre rc
2.0.0-rc.2
$ gitversioned version --next
2.0.0
```

### Nothing to release

When the commits since the last release ask for nothing, there is no next
version and the exit code is 1, so a workflow can skip the release:

```console
$ git tag v2.0.0 && echo ci >> notes.txt && git commit -qam "ci: cache the venv"
$ gitversioned version --next
fail  Nothing to release since 2.0.0: no commit since is a feat, a fix or another releasable type.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned version --next --bump patch
2.0.1
```

### Below 1.0

Before 1.0.0 every level shifts down one: a breaking change is a minor release
and a feature a patch release.

```console
$ git init -q ../early && cd ../early && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: start" && git tag v0.3.0
$ cd ../early && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: add a thing" && gitversioned version --next
0.3.1
$ cd ../early && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat!: drop the old thing" && gitversioned version --next
0.4.0
$ cd ../early && gitversioned version --next --bump major
1.0.0
```

## How it works

- The rules are fixed: there is no bump setting. The
  [concepts guide](https://markurtz.github.io/git-versioned/guides/concepts/)
  lists every type and its level.
- Overrides win in this order: a `VERSION` argument or `--bump`, then
  `GITVERSIONED__BUMP`, then the `release:major`, `release:minor` and
  `release:patch` labels on pull requests (see
  [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md)).

## Next

- [release-local](../release-local/README.md) to turn the next version into a release.
- [commit-checks](../commit-checks/README.md) to keep commit subjects parseable.
````

## File: examples/npm-workspace/README.md

````markdown
# An npm workspace

Two npm packages on one version: a published library and a private app that
depends on it, under a private workspace root with no version. Changesets and
release-please keep internal dependency ranges in step on a release; here
`gitversioned version --write` does it from the tag on every build.

| Level        | Shows                                                         | Needs     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |
| Intermediate | `version --write`, internal dependencies, `[[targets]]` `key`, `npm pack` | git, npm  |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v2.0.0
$ gitversioned version --write
2.0.0
  packages/app/package.json   2.0.0
  packages/core/package.json  2.0.0
  pnpm-workspace.yaml         2.0.0
$ git diff -U0 | grep '^[-+][^-+]'
-  "version": "0.0.0",
+  "version": "2.0.0",
-    "@demo/core": "^0.0.0"
+    "@demo/core": "^2.0.0"
-  "version": "0.0.0",
+  "version": "2.0.0",
-  "@demo/core": 0.0.0
+  "@demo/core": 2.0.0
```

The root `package.json` has no version and is left alone. The app's
`^0.0.0` range on the library became `^2.0.0`, keeping its operator, so npm
links the workspace copy and the packed library carries the release:

```console
$ npm install --offline --no-audit --no-fund --silent && node packages/app/index.js
hello app
$ npm pack --dry-run --json -w @demo/core | grep '"version"'
    "version": "2.0.0",
```

`npm version` would commit and tag by itself; here the tag is the only source,
and the stamped files never count as a dirty tree:

```console
$ gitversioned version
2.0.0
$ git checkout -q . && rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
```

Pre-releases are spelled the npm way, and `--json` says it is one, so a release
job can publish it to the
`next` dist-tag instead of `latest`:

```console
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: try a new API" && git tag v2.1.0-rc.1
$ gitversioned version --write >/dev/null && grep '"version"' packages/core/package.json
  "version": "2.1.0-rc.1",
$ gitversioned version --json | grep -E '"(type|prerelease)"'
  "type": "release",
  "prerelease": true,
```

## How it works

- Every `package.json` with a `version` is found by discovery. When a repository
  has several, dependencies between them that name a single version (`1.2.0`,
  `^1.2.0`, `~1.2.0`) follow the release; `workspace:` and `*` ranges are left
  for the package manager.
- [`gitversioned.toml`](gitversioned.toml) lists the pnpm catalog entry, a
  dotted `key` in a YAML file.
- [`package.json`](package.json) at the root is private and has no version.

## Next

- [monorepo-packages](../monorepo-packages/README.md) to give a package its own tags.
- [docker](../docker/README.md) for image tags from the same version.
````

## File: examples/polyglot/README.md

````markdown
# One version for every manifest

One repository holding a Python package at the root, a Cargo workspace, a Helm
chart, a citation file, a Dockerfile, a docs page that names the version, and an
npm package with its own release line. One command stamps them all, each in the
spelling its ecosystem expects.

| Level    | Shows                                                                     | Needs  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Advanced | discovery, `version --write`, `--dry-run`, `[[targets]]`, `[packages]`, `.config/gitversioned.toml` | Python |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.4.0 && git tag web-v0.9.0
$ gitversioned check | sed -n '1,3p'
ok    config        .config/gitversioned.toml
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v1.4.0
ok    targets       CITATION.cff, Dockerfile, charts/demo/Chart.yaml, crates/cli/Cargo.toml, crates/core/Cargo.toml, src/demo/version.py, Cargo.lock, docs/install.md, packages/web/package.json
```

### Preview, then write

`--dry-run` prints the diff and changes nothing:

```console
$ gitversioned version --write --dry-run | sed -n '1,12p'
1.4.0
--- a/CITATION.cff
+++ b/CITATION.cff
@@ -4,5 +4,5 @@
 type: software
 authors:
   - name: "The demo authors"
-version: 0.0.0
-date-released: "2026-01-01"
+version: 1.4.0
+date-released: "2026-11-25"
--- a/Dockerfile
$ git status --short
```

Without it, every target is stamped:

```console
$ gitversioned version --write
1.4.0
  CITATION.cff            1.4.0
  Dockerfile              1.4.0
  charts/demo/Chart.yaml  1.4.0
  crates/cli/Cargo.toml   1.4.0
  crates/core/Cargo.toml  1.4.0
  src/demo/version.py     1.4.0
  Cargo.lock              1.4.0
  docs/install.md         1.4.0
$ grep -h -E '^version|version = "=|appVersion|image.version|demo-cli@' Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml charts/demo/Chart.yaml Dockerfile docs/install.md
version = "1.4.0"
demo-core = { path = "../core", version = "=1.4.0" }
version = "1.4.0"
version: 1.4.0
appVersion: "1.4.0"
      org.opencontainers.image.version="1.4.0"
cargo install demo-cli@1.4.0
$ grep -E '^(version|date-released)' CITATION.cff
version: 1.4.0
date-released: "2026-11-25"
$ grep '"version"' packages/web/package.json
  "version": "0.0.0",
```

The web package was left at `0.0.0`: it has its own tag, so the repository's
version is not its version. Stamping it is a separate run:

```console
$ gitversioned version -p web --write
0.9.0
  packages/web/package.json  0.9.0
```

The stamped files do not make the tree dirty, so the version is still the
release:

```console
$ gitversioned version
1.4.0
$ git checkout -q .
```

### Its own release line

Commits under `packages/web` belong to the web package, and the rest of the
repository does not see them:

```console
$ echo 'export const name = "web";' > packages/web/index.js && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(web): shorter name"
$ gitversioned version -p web --next
0.9.1
$ gitversioned version --next
fail  Nothing to release since 1.4.0: no commit since is a feat, a fix or another releasable type.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned release -p web | sed -n '1,3p'
release   0.9.1  (patch, from commits, from 0.9.0)
tag       web-v0.9.1
files     packages/web/CHANGELOG.md, packages/web/package.json
```

## How it works

- Discovery finds `src/demo/version.py` (generated, never committed), each
  crate's `Cargo.toml` with its path-dependency pins, `Cargo.lock`,
  `charts/demo/Chart.yaml` (`version` and `appVersion`), `CITATION.cff`
  (`version`, and `date-released` on a release), the OCI version label in the
  `Dockerfile`, and `packages/web/package.json`.
- [`.config/gitversioned.toml`](.config/gitversioned.toml) adds the docs page
  as a `pattern` target, limits scopes, and gives `packages/web` its own tag.

## Next

- [template-polyglot](../template-polyglot/README.md) for the full layout markurtz/template renders.
- [monorepo-packages](../monorepo-packages/README.md) for more on `[packages]`.
````

## File: examples/python-api/README.md

````markdown
# The Python API

The command line is a thin layer over a small Python API: `load_config`,
`resolve`, `stamp`, `plan_release` and `get_version`, plus `Version` and the
error classes. [`main.py`](main.py) calls each one and asserts the answer, so it
exits non-zero if the API ever disagrees with this page.

| Level        | Shows                                                                   | Needs  |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Intermediate | `load_config`, `resolve`, `stamp`, `plan_release`, `get_version`, `Version` | Python |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v0.8.0
$ echo "x = 1" > src/apidemo/parse.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): parse empty input"
$ python main.py
version  0.8.1.dev20261125+dae4574 (dev, from tag)
semver   0.8.1-dev.20261125+dae4574
tag      v0.8.0, 1 commit(s) since, sha dae4574
stamp    src/apidemo/version.py -> 0.8.1.dev20261125+dae4574 (commit=False)
release  0.8.1 as v0.8.1 (patch, from commits, from 0.8.0)
## [0.8.1] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed

- **core**: parse empty input
```

The same answers from the command line:

```console
$ gitversioned version && gitversioned release | sed -n '1,2p'
0.8.1.dev20261125+dae4574
release   0.8.1  (patch, from commits, from 0.8.0)
tag       v0.8.1
```

## How it works

[`main.py`](main.py) in reading order:

1. `load_config(root)` finds the settings home (none here) and returns a
   `Config`.
1. `resolve(config)` returns a `Resolved`: the version, its type and source, the
   tag, the distance and the commit.
1. `stamp(config, resolved, dry_run=True)` returns one `Change` per target
   without writing; without `dry_run` it writes them.
1. `plan_release(config)` returns a `ReleasePlan`, or raises
   `NothingToReleaseError` when nothing is releasable.

The [API guide](https://markurtz.github.io/git-versioned/guides/api/) documents
every function.

## Next

- [release-local](../release-local/README.md) for the same plan from the command line.
````

## File: examples/release-local/README.md

````markdown
# Releasing from a terminal

The whole release, by hand: preview the plan, write the changelog and the
committed manifests, commit, and tag. A workflow runs the same steps with the
same checks (see [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md)).

| Level        | Shows                                                                        | Needs |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| Intermediate | `release`, `--write`, `--tag`, `VERSION`, `annotated`, `[Unreleased]`, `check --tag` | git   |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates. A bare repository next to the example stands in for GitHub.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first public release" && git tag v1.2.0
$ git init -q --bare ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git && git push -q origin main v1.2.0
$ echo "a = 1" > src/relay/a.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(cli): add --explain (#41)"
$ echo "b = 1" > src/relay/b.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): peel annotated tags (#40)"
$ echo "c = 1" > src/relay/c.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "chore(deps): bump ruff (#39)"
$ echo "d = 1" > src/relay/d.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "docs: describe the plan (#42)"
```

### The plan

`release` changes nothing. It prints the version, the tag, the files a release
would touch and the changelog section. Maintenance commits (`chore`, `ci`,
`test`) are left out, and `docs` goes under Changed:

```console
$ gitversioned release
release   1.3.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.2.0)
tag       v1.3.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Changed

- describe the plan (#42)

### Fixed

- **core**: peel annotated tags (#40)

### Security

- Pin the build image by digest.

Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.
$ git status --short
```

`--json` gives a script the same plan:

```console
$ gitversioned release --json
{
  "stage": "plan",
  "version": "1.3.0",
  "semver": "1.3.0",
  "previous": "1.2.0",
  "tag": "v1.3.0",
  "level": "minor, from commits, from 1.2.0",
  "files": [
    "CHANGELOG.md",
    "CITATION.cff"
  ],
  "changed": [],
  "changelog": "## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25\n\n### Added\n\n- **cli**: add --explain (#41)\n\n### Changed\n\n- describe the plan (#42)\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **core**: peel annotated tags (#40)\n\n### Security\n\n- Pin the build image by digest.\n"
}
```

### Write, commit, tag

`--write` applies the plan to the working tree. The lines under
`## [Unreleased]` move into the new section, as Keep a Changelog asks, and the
citation file gets the new version and date:

```console
$ gitversioned release --write
release   1.3.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.2.0)
tag       v1.3.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Changed

- describe the plan (#42)

### Fixed

- **core**: peel annotated tags (#40)

### Security

- Pin the build image by digest.

Wrote CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff.
$ git diff CITATION.cff | tail -4
-version: "1.2.0"
-date-released: "2026-01-15"
+version: "1.3.0"
+date-released: "2026-11-25"
$ sed -n '6,30p' CHANGELOG.md
## [Unreleased]

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Changed

- describe the plan (#42)

### Fixed

- **core**: peel annotated tags (#40)

### Security

- Pin the build image by digest.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-01-15

### Added

- First public release.
```

Commit it with the release title, then `--tag` tags that commit and pushes the
tag. Because `annotated = true` is set, the tag message is the changelog
section:

```console
$ git commit -qam "release: v1.3.0" && git push -q origin main
$ gitversioned release --tag
tag       v1.3.0 at 1252338, pushed
$ git ls-remote --tags origin | sed 's/^[0-9a-f]*\t//' | grep -v '\^{}'
refs/tags/v1.2.0
refs/tags/v1.3.0
$ git tag -l --format='%(contents)' v1.3.0
## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Changed

- describe the plan (#42)

### Fixed

- **core**: peel annotated tags (#40)

### Security

- Pin the build image by digest.

$ gitversioned version
1.3.0
```

Once the tag exists there is nothing left to release:

```console
$ gitversioned release
fail  Nothing to release since 1.3.0: no commit since is a feat, a fix or another releasable type.
[exit 1]
```

### Tag by hand

With a `VERSION`, `--tag` tags the current commit by hand, like the template's
`release-manual` workflow. It runs the checks of `check --tag`: the version is
newer than every release, and the changelog holds its section.

```console
$ echo "e = 1" > src/relay/e.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): one more fix" && git push -q origin main
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.3.0
fail  tag  tag v1.3.0 already exists at 1252338.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned release 1.2.9 --tag
fail  1.2.9 is not newer than v1.3.0.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned release 1.3.1 --tag
fail  CHANGELOG.md has no [1.3.1] section. Run `gitversioned release 1.3.1 --write` and commit it first.
[exit 1]
```

Write the section first, commit it, and the same command tags:

```console
$ gitversioned release 1.3.1 --write && git commit -qam "release: v1.3.1"
release   1.3.1  (set by VERSION, from 1.3.0)
tag       v1.3.1
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff

## [1.3.1] - 2026-11-25

### Fixed

- **core**: one more fix

Wrote CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff.
$ gitversioned check --tag v1.3.1
ok    tag        1.3.1, newer than v1.3.0
ok    changelog  CHANGELOG.md has the section
$ gitversioned release 1.3.1 --tag
tag       v1.3.1 at 098285d, pushed
$ gitversioned version
1.3.1
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) sets one key, `annotated = true`, under
  `[tool.gitversioned]`; lightweight tags are the default.
- [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md) starts with an `[Unreleased]` section written
  by hand. Releases insert their section below it and never edit older ones.
- [`CITATION.cff`](CITATION.cff) is found by discovery; its `version` and
  `date-released` follow each release.
- `changelog = false` turns the changelog off, and `changelog = "docs/changes.md"`
  moves it.

## Next

- [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md) for the same release through a reviewed pull request.
- [next-version](../next-version/README.md) for how the level is chosen.
````

## File: examples/release-pr/README.md

````markdown
# The release pull request

The reviewed release, as release-please and release-plz run it: on every push to
`main`, `gitversioned release --pr` rebuilds the `release/next` branch from
`main` and opens or updates one pull request holding the changelog section and
the stamped files. Merging it is the release decision, and
`gitversioned release --tag` tags the merge.

| Level    | Shows                                                                      | Needs                     |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Advanced | `release --pr`, `release --tag`, `release:rc` and `release:<level>` labels, `## Changelog` blocks | git, `gh` signed in |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. Here a bare
repository stands in for GitHub and a stand-in `gh` keeps pull requests in a
JSON file; with a real remote and a signed-in `gh` the commands are the same.
Squash merges are done with git, as GitHub would do them.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first release" && git tag v1.2.0
$ git init -q --bare ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git && git push -q -u origin main v1.2.0
```

### Feature pull requests

Two feature pull requests are merged. The second rewrites its changelog entry
with a `## Changelog` block in its body, which replaces the title in the
release notes:

```console
$ echo "a = 1" > src/beacon/a.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(cli): add --explain (#41)" && git push -q
$ git switch -q -c fix-tags && echo "b = 1" > src/beacon/b.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): peel tags" && git push -q -u origin fix-tags
$ gh pr create --base main --head fix-tags --title "fix(core): peel annotated tags" --body $'Peels tags.\n\n## Changelog\n\n### Fixed\n\n- Annotated tags now resolve to their commit, so `version` agrees with `git describe`.'
https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/57
$ git switch -q main && git merge -q --squash fix-tags >/dev/null && git commit -qm "fix(core): peel annotated tags (#57)" && git push -q && gh pr merge 57 --squash
```

### Open the release pull request

```console
$ gitversioned release --pr
release   1.3.0
branch    release/next  (rebuilt from main)
commit    release: v1.3.0
pr        #58 opened  https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/58
$ gh pr view 58 --jq .title
release: v1.3.0
$ gh pr view 58 --jq .body
## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Fixed

- **core**: Annotated tags now resolve to their commit, so `version` agrees with `git describe`. (#57)

---
Merging this pull request releases `v1.3.0`. Add the `release:rc` label to make it a release candidate.

$ git log -1 --format=%s origin/release/next && git diff --stat main origin/release/next
release: v1.3.0
 CHANGELOG.md | 10 ++++++++++
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+)
```

Nothing changed on `main` itself:

```console
$ git status --short && git log -1 --format=%s
fix(core): peel annotated tags (#57)
```

### Keep it up to date

Every push to `main` rebuilds the branch from scratch, so the pull request never
drifts from `main` and never reverts a file:

```console
$ echo "c = 1" > src/beacon/c.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "perf(core): cache tag lookups (#45)" && git push -q
$ gitversioned release --pr
release   1.3.0
branch    release/next  (rebuilt from main)
commit    release: v1.3.0
pr        #58 updated  https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/58
$ gh pr view 58 --jq .body | grep -c "^- "
3
```

### Release candidates

The `release:rc` label on the release pull request makes the next refresh a
release candidate:

```console
$ gh pr edit 58 --add-label release:rc >/dev/null
$ gitversioned release --pr
release   1.3.0rc1
branch    release/next  (rebuilt from main)
commit    release: v1.3.0-rc.1
pr        #58 updated  https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/58
$ gh pr view 58 --jq .title
release: v1.3.0-rc.1
```

Merging it releases the candidate. Until the tag exists, `release --pr` waits
instead of opening the next release:

```console
$ git merge -q --squash origin/release/next >/dev/null && git commit -qm "release: v1.3.0-rc.1 (#58)" && git push -q && gh pr merge 58 --squash
$ gitversioned release --pr
fail  HEAD is the merged release commit for v1.3.0-rc.1, which is not tagged yet. Run release --tag first.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned release --tag
tag       v1.3.0-rc.1 at 94eaaf3, pushed
$ gitversioned version
1.3.0rc1
```

### The final release

The next run opens a new pull request for the final release. Its section takes
over the candidate's entries and replaces the candidate's section:

```console
$ gitversioned release --pr
release   1.3.0
branch    release/next  (rebuilt from main)
commit    release: v1.3.0
pr        #59 opened  https://github.com/acme/acme/pull/59
$ gh pr view 59 --jq .title
release: v1.3.0
$ git show origin/release/next:CHANGELOG.md | sed -n '6,24p'
## [Unreleased]

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **cli**: add --explain (#41)

### Changed

- **core**: cache tag lookups (#45)

### Fixed

- **core**: Annotated tags now resolve to their commit, so `version` agrees with `git describe`. (#57)

## [1.2.0] - 2026-10-01

### Added
```

A `release:major`, `release:minor` or `release:patch` label on a feature pull
request merged since the last release overrides the level:

```console
$ gh pr edit 57 --add-label release:major >/dev/null
$ gitversioned release --pr | grep "^release"
release   2.0.0
$ gh pr edit 57 --remove-label release:major >/dev/null && gitversioned release --pr | grep "^release"
release   1.3.0
```

Merge it and tag it:

```console
$ git merge -q --squash origin/release/next >/dev/null && git commit -qm "release: v1.3.0 (#59)" && git push -q && gh pr merge 59 --squash
$ gitversioned release --tag
tag       v1.3.0 at a0f0635, pushed
$ git ls-remote --tags origin | sed 's/^[0-9a-f]*\t//'
refs/tags/v1.2.0
refs/tags/v1.3.0
refs/tags/v1.3.0-rc.1
```

## How it works

- The branch, title and labels are fixed: `release/next`, `release: vX.Y.Z`, and
  the `release` label; `release:rc` asks for a candidate.
- `release --pr` refuses to run on any branch but `branch` (`main` by default)
  and on a dirty tree, so a release never carries unmerged work.
- Entries come from pull request titles when `gh` can read them, and from
  squash commit subjects otherwise. `chore`, `ci` and `test` are left out.
- The [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) example runs these steps in
  workflows.

## Next

- [release-local](../release-local/README.md) for the same release without GitHub.
- [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) for the workflows that run it.
````

## File: examples/rust-workspace/README.md

````markdown
# A Rust workspace

A Cargo workspace with no Python at all: three crates on one version, an
inherited `version.workspace = true`, internal dependencies pinned by version,
and a committed `Cargo.lock`. The manifests stay at `0.0.0` in git, and
`gitversioned version --write` stamps the tag's version before a build, as
cargo-release and release-plz do when they cut a release.

| Level        | Shows                                                                     | Needs       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| Intermediate | `version --write`, `[workspace.package]`, `[workspace.dependencies]`, `Cargo.lock` | git, Cargo  |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

With no Python project in the folder, versions print in SemVer:

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.4.0
$ gitversioned version
1.4.0
$ gitversioned version --write
1.4.0
  Cargo.toml               1.4.0
  crates/extra/Cargo.toml  1.4.0
  Cargo.lock               1.4.0
$ git diff --stat
 Cargo.lock              | 6 +++---
 Cargo.toml              | 4 ++--
 crates/extra/Cargo.toml | 4 ++--
 3 files changed, 7 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

Every value Cargo checks moved together, so a locked, offline build works and
each crate reports the release:

```console
$ git diff crates/extra/Cargo.toml Cargo.toml | grep '^[-+][^-+]'
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "1.4.0"
-demo-core = { path = "crates/core", version = "0.0.0" }
+demo-core = { path = "crates/core", version = "1.4.0" }
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "1.4.0"
-demo-core = { path = "../core", version = "0.0.0" }
+demo-core = { path = "../core", version = "1.4.0" }
$ cargo run -q --locked --offline -p demo-cli
demo-cli 1.4.0 (core 1.4.0)
```

The stamp is not a change to the source: the version is still the clean
release, not a dirty development build.

```console
$ gitversioned version
1.4.0
$ git checkout -q .
```

A development build gets a SemVer pre-release with the commit hash as build
metadata. Requirements on sibling crates leave the build metadata out, which
Cargo would otherwise warn about:

```console
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "fix(core): tighten checks"
$ gitversioned version --write >/dev/null && grep -h 'version = ' Cargo.toml crates/extra/Cargo.toml
version = "1.4.1-dev.20261125+ea5ecdd"
demo-core = { path = "crates/core", version = "1.4.1-dev.20261125" }
version = "1.4.1-dev.20261125+ea5ecdd"
demo-core = { path = "../core", version = "1.4.1-dev.20261125" }
$ cargo run -q --locked --offline -p demo-cli
demo-cli 1.4.1-dev.20261125+ea5ecdd (core 1.4.1-dev.20261125+ea5ecdd)
```

## How it works

- [`Cargo.toml`](Cargo.toml) holds `[workspace.package] version` and the
  `[workspace.dependencies]` entry for the core. Both are found by discovery.
- [`crates/extra/Cargo.toml`](crates/extra/Cargo.toml) spells its version out
  and depends on the core by path and version; both values are stamped.
- `Cargo.lock` entries of the workspace's own crates are rewritten in place;
  entries of other crates are never touched.
- [cargo-release](https://github.com/crate-ci/cargo-release) and
  [release-plz](https://release-plz.dev) edit the same fields; gitversioned
  does it from the tag on every build, so nothing is committed between
  releases.

## Next

- [maturin](../maturin/README.md) for a Rust crate built as a Python extension.
- [monorepo-packages](../monorepo-packages/README.md) for crates with their own tags.
````

## File: examples/setuptools/README.md

````markdown
# setuptools from pyproject.toml

A setuptools package whose version comes from its git tags. Listing
`gitversioned` in `build-system.requires` is the opt-in; settings live in the
`[tool.gitversioned]` table of the same file.

| Level    | Build backend | Needs                            |
| -------- | ------------- | -------------------------------- |
| Beginner | setuptools    | Python, `build`, `setuptools>=64` |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(core): first version" && git tag v2.1.0
$ gitversioned version
2.1.0
$ python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_setuptools-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
$ unzip -p dist/demo_setuptools-2.1.0-py3-none-any.whl demo_setuptools/version.py | grep "^__version__"
__version__ = version = "2.1.0"
$ git status --short
```

The settings in `pyproject.toml` limit commit scopes to `core` and `docs`:

```console
$ gitversioned check "feat(core): add a thing"
ok
$ gitversioned check "feat(web): add a page"
fail  title  unknown scope 'web'. Scopes: core, docs.
[exit 1]
$ gitversioned version --explain | tail -1
config    pyproject.toml [tool.gitversioned]  (1 key set, 13 defaults)
```

A commit after the tag builds a development version:

```console
$ echo "x = 1" > src/demo_setuptools/extra.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(core): add extra"
$ rm -rf dist build && python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
demo_setuptools-2.1.1.dev20261125+474e126-py3-none-any.whl
```

`--no-isolation` is only here because the test runs against the gitversioned
under test; a normal `python -m build` installs it from PyPI.

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml): `gitversioned` in `build-system.requires`,
  `dynamic = ["version"]`, and a `[tool.gitversioned]` table with `scopes`.
- The build writes `src/demo_setuptools/version.py`, which
  [`.gitignore`](.gitignore) keeps out of git.

## Next

- [setuptools-legacy](../setuptools-legacy/README.md) for `setup.cfg` and `setup.py`.
- [commit-checks](../commit-checks/README.md) for everything `check` does.
````

## File: examples/setuptools-legacy/README.md

````markdown
# setuptools from setup.cfg and setup.py

Older setuptools projects keep their metadata in `setup.cfg` and call `setup()`
from `setup.py`, with no `pyproject.toml`. `setup(gitversioned=True)` turns the
integration on, and the `[tool:gitversioned]` table in `setup.cfg` holds the
settings.

| Level    | Build backend         | Needs                    |
| -------- | --------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Beginner | setuptools (setup.py) | Python, `build`, `setuptools` |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v0.4.2
$ gitversioned version
0.4.2
$ python -m build --wheel --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
legacy_app-0.4.2-py3-none-any.whl
$ gitversioned version --explain | tail -1
config    setup.cfg [tool:gitversioned]  (1 key set, 13 defaults)
```

Before the first tag, the fallback from `setup.cfg` is the base:

```console
$ git tag -d v0.4.2 >/dev/null && gitversioned version
0.0.1.dev20261125+34335b3
```

## How it works

- [`setup.py`](setup.py) passes `gitversioned=True` to `setup()`.
- [`setup.cfg`](setup.cfg) holds the metadata and a `[tool:gitversioned]` table.
- `version.py` is generated only for projects with a `pyproject.toml`; here
  the version is in the wheel's metadata (`importlib.metadata.version`).
- With no `pyproject.toml`, the build runs setuptools' legacy backend, which
  needs gitversioned installed where the build runs (pip's
  `--no-build-isolation`, or a `pyproject.toml` that lists it in
  `build-system.requires`).

## Next

- [setuptools](../setuptools/README.md) for the `pyproject.toml` form.
````

## File: examples/static-version/README.md

````markdown
# Static versions for uv_build

uv_build, like Flit's core backend and Poetry's, reads a static
`[project].version` and has no plugin hook. gitversioned writes the version
into `pyproject.toml` before the build, then the build names everything for it.

| Level        | Build backend | Needs                  |
| ------------ | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| Intermediate | uv_build      | Python, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version" && git tag v1.4.0
$ echo '"""Parsing."""' > src/demo_uv/parse.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: parse input"
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v1.4.0
ok    targets       pyproject.toml
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

A nightly or a test build stamps the development version, builds, and puts the
file back, so nothing is committed:

```console
$ gitversioned version --write
1.4.1.dev20261125+bd86c17
  pyproject.toml  1.4.1.dev20261125+bd86c17
$ uv build -q 2>&1; ls dist
demo_uv-1.4.1.dev20261125+bd86c17-py3-none-any.whl
demo_uv-1.4.1.dev20261125+bd86c17.tar.gz
$ git checkout -q pyproject.toml && rm -rf dist && git status --short
```

A release writes the next version and the changelog. Commit them and tag that
commit, so the tag holds the released number and builds without gitversioned:

```console
$ gitversioned release --write
release   1.5.0  (minor, from commits, from 1.4.0)
tag       v1.5.0
files     CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml

## [1.5.0] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- parse input

Wrote CHANGELOG.md, pyproject.toml.
$ git add -A && git commit -qm "release: v1.5.0" && git tag v1.5.0 && grep '^version' pyproject.toml
version = "1.5.0"
$ uv build -q 2>&1; ls dist
demo_uv-1.5.0-py3-none-any.whl
demo_uv-1.5.0.tar.gz
$ gitversioned version && git status --short
1.5.0
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) has a static `version = "0.0.0"`, which is
  only a placeholder: gitversioned finds it because `version` is not listed in
  `dynamic`, and lists `pyproject.toml` as a target.
- `version --write` writes the version and leaves the file changed, so run it in
  a throwaway checkout or restore the file after the build.
- `release --write` writes the same file and the changelog, and you commit
  them. The tag on that commit then matches the version in the file, so the
  sdist and anyone building from the tag get 1.5.0 without gitversioned.
- On a development checkout, `version --write` gives one patch above the tag
  whatever the commits are; `version --write --next` stamps the next release
  number instead.
- [`src/demo_uv/__init__.py`](src/demo_uv/__init__.py) reads `__version__` from
  the installed metadata, since uv_build writes no version module.

## Next

- [hatchling](../hatchling/README.md) for a backend with a build hook, where
  nothing is written to the tree.
- [release-local](../release-local/README.md) for the release commit in detail.
````

## File: examples/template-polyglot/README.md

````markdown
# A template polyglot repository

The manifests of a [markurtz/template](https://github.com/markurtz/template)
polyglot render, Python primary, copied from the generator's snapshot: the root
hatchling package, a virtual Cargo workspace with `workspace.package` and
`workspace.dependencies`, the maturin binding, the wasm npm package, a pnpm
workspace with private apps, the desktop app's own Tauri workspace, the API's
private `pyproject.toml`, a cargo-fuzz harness, the example legs and
`CITATION.cff`. The lockfiles are trimmed to a few entries, and the source files
are left out.

`gitversioned version --write` replaces the template's `release:stamp` task, and
`release --write` its release pull request contents.

| Level    | Shows                                                                     | Needs  |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Advanced | discovery across every block, scopes from `.config/blocks.toml`, what is never stamped, builds that stay clean | Python |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first release" && git tag v0.3.0
$ git init -q --bare ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git && git push -q -u origin main v0.3.0
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        pyproject.toml [tool.gitversioned]
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v0.3.0
ok    targets       CITATION.cff, Cargo.toml, apps/desktop/package.json, apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml, apps/web/package.json, crates/wasm/package.json, packages/client/package.json, src/template_polyglot/version.py, Cargo.lock, apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock
ok    scopes        core, oci, python, api, rust, cli, node, contract, db, web, desktop, docs, notebooks, python-ext, wasm, deps, deps-dev, ci, release
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

### Pull request titles

`pr.yml` checks the title with `gitversioned check "$PR_TITLE"`. The scopes are
the block names in `.config/blocks.toml` plus `deps`, `deps-dev`, `ci` and
`release`:

```console
$ gitversioned check "feat(wasm): export count_words"
ok
$ gitversioned check "chore(deps-dev): bump vitest"
ok
$ gitversioned check "feat(frontend): dark mode"
fail  title  unknown scope 'frontend'. Scopes: core, oci, python, api, rust, cli, node, contract, db, web, desktop, docs, notebooks, python-ext, wasm, deps, deps-dev, ci, release.
[exit 1]
```

### Stamp a build

A build or publish job between releases stamps the development version where
`release:stamp` did. Every manifest that ships gets it, each in its own
spelling; the workspace's path dependency follows; `Cargo.lock` changes only the
workspace's own crates:

```console
$ echo "x = 1" > src/template_polyglot/stats.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(web): word cloud (#21)"
$ gitversioned version --write
0.3.1.dev20261125+5a80275
  CITATION.cff                       0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  Cargo.toml                         0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  apps/desktop/package.json          0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml  0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  apps/web/package.json              0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  crates/wasm/package.json           0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  packages/client/package.json       0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  src/template_polyglot/version.py   0.3.1.dev20261125+5a80275
  Cargo.lock                         0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
  apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock  0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275
$ git diff Cargo.toml Cargo.lock | grep '^[-+][^-+]'
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275"
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275"
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275"
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275"
-version = "0.0.0"
+version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125+5a80275"
-template-polyglot-core = { path = "crates/core", version = "0.0.0" }
+template-polyglot-core = { path = "crates/core", version = "0.3.1-dev.20261125" }
```

Some manifests are left alone: the example legs under `examples/`, the fuzz
harness (`cargo-fuzz = true`), and the API, whose `Private :: Do Not Upload`
classifier says it never ships. The stamped files do not make the tree dirty,
so the build that follows still gets a clean version:

```console
$ git status --short
 M CITATION.cff
 M Cargo.lock
 M Cargo.toml
 M apps/desktop/package.json
 M apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock
 M apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
 M apps/web/package.json
 M crates/wasm/package.json
 M packages/client/package.json
$ grep -c '"0.0.0"' Cargo.lock && grep '^version' apps/api/pyproject.toml crates/core/fuzz/Cargo.toml examples/text-stats/rust/Cargo.toml
1
apps/api/pyproject.toml:version = "0.0.0"
crates/core/fuzz/Cargo.toml:version = "0.0.0"
examples/text-stats/rust/Cargo.toml:version = "0.0.0"
$ gitversioned version
0.3.1.dev20261125+5a80275
$ git checkout -q . && git status --short
```

### Release

`release --write` writes the same files at the release version, folds the
`[Unreleased]` lines into the new section, and adds `version` and
`date-released` to `CITATION.cff`. Committing them means the tagged commit names
its own version in every manifest, so `cargo publish`, `npm publish` and
maturin need no stamp step on the tag:

```console
$ gitversioned release --write | sed -n '1,3p'
release   0.3.1  (minor, a patch below 1.0.0, from commits, from 0.3.0)
tag       v0.3.1
files     CHANGELOG.md, CITATION.cff, Cargo.toml, apps/desktop/package.json, apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml, apps/web/package.json, crates/wasm/package.json, packages/client/package.json, Cargo.lock, apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.lock
$ sed -n '/^## \[0.3.1\]/,/^## \[0.3.0\]/p' CHANGELOG.md
## [0.3.1] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **core**: Initial repository generated from [markurtz/template](https://github.com/markurtz/template).
- **web**: word cloud (#21)
$ git diff CITATION.cff | grep '^+[^+]'
+version: "0.3.1"
+date-released: "2026-11-25"
$ git commit -qam "release: v0.3.1" && git push -q && gitversioned release --tag
tag       v0.3.1 at d09b581, pushed
$ gitversioned version && gitversioned check --tag v0.3.1 | sed -n '1p'
0.3.1
ok    tag        0.3.1 at HEAD, newer than v0.3.0
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) adds one table to the rendered file:
  `[tool.gitversioned] scopes = [".config/blocks.toml", "deps", "deps-dev",
  "ci", "release"]`. The build requirement is `gitversioned>=0.4`.
- Discovery reads every tracked manifest except those under `examples/`,
  `tests/` and other fixture folders, a nested `CITATION.cff`, a cargo-fuzz
  harness and a Python project marked `Private :: Do Not Upload`.
- `crates/*` inherit `version.workspace = true`, so only the root `Cargo.toml`
  changes. The maturin binding in `crates/python-ext` reads that version.
- The desktop app's `src-tauri` is its own workspace with its own `Cargo.lock`;
  Tauri names the installers after its `version`.
- The root `package.json` is private and has no version, so it is left alone.
- The changelog in the render groups entries by scope first; gitversioned reads
  those entries and writes the new section by type, with the scope in bold.

## What the template changes

- `release:stamp` becomes `gitversioned version --write`, and `release:verify`
  becomes `gitversioned check --tag`; see
  [template-python](../template-python/README.md).
- Manifests hold the last release's version between releases instead of
  `0.0.0`, since `release --write` commits them.
- `pr.yml`'s title check becomes `gitversioned check "$PR_TITLE"`.

## Next

- [template-python](../template-python/README.md) for the release tasks.
- [polyglot](../polyglot/README.md) for Helm, Docker and `[packages]`.
````

## File: examples/template-python/README.md

````markdown
# A template python-size repository

The parts of a [markurtz/template](https://github.com/markurtz/template)
python-size render that gitversioned touches: hatchling with the build hook, no
settings, a Keep a Changelog file with an `[Unreleased]` section, and the
`release:verify`, `release:notes` and `release:manual` tasks behind
`release.yml` and `release-manual.yml`. The tasks are the mise file tasks from
[`.mise/tasks/release/`](.mise/tasks/release), run here directly with bash.

| Level    | Shows                                                         | Needs                        |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Advanced | zero config, `[Unreleased]` folding, `check --tag`, `release VERSION --tag` | git, Python, `build`, `hatchling` |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. A bare repository
stands in for GitHub.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first release" && git tag v0.1.0
$ git init -q --bare ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git && git push -q -u origin main v0.1.0
$ gitversioned check
ok    config        defaults
ok    git           full history, 1 release tag, latest v0.1.0
ok    targets       src/text_stats/version.py
warn  archive file  .git_archival.txt is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. Run `gitversioned init`.
warn  github        gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in the changelog are unavailable.
```

Pull requests merge with Conventional Commit titles. A build of `main` is a
development version, and the tree stays clean because `version.py` is ignored:

```console
$ echo "a = 1" > src/text_stats/lines.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat(python): count blank lines (#7)" && git push -q
$ echo "b = 1" > src/text_stats/words.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "fix(python): count hyphenated words once (#8)" && git push -q
$ python -m build --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist && git status --short
text_stats-0.1.1.dev20261125+a25a8d6-py3-none-any.whl
text_stats-0.1.1.dev20261125+a25a8d6.tar.gz
```

### Prepare the release

Until the release pull request is turned on, a maintainer writes the release in
a pull request of its own. Below 1.0.0 every level shifts down one, so the
feature makes a patch release. The `[Unreleased]` entries written by hand join
the entries from the commits, and `[Unreleased]` is left empty:

```console
$ git switch -q -c release-0.1.1 && gitversioned release --write && git diff --stat
release   0.1.1  (minor, a patch below 1.0.0, from commits, from 0.1.0)
tag       v0.1.1
files     CHANGELOG.md

## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **python**: count blank lines (#7)

### Deprecated

- `count_words()` is deprecated; use `count()`.

### Fixed

- **python**: count hyphenated words once (#8)

Wrote CHANGELOG.md.
 CHANGELOG.md | 10 ++++++++++
 1 file changed, 10 insertions(+)
$ sed -n '8,30p' CHANGELOG.md
## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.1] - 2026-11-25

### Added

- **python**: count blank lines (#7)

### Deprecated

- `count_words()` is deprecated; use `count()`.

### Fixed

- **python**: count hyphenated words once (#8)

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-01

### Added

- First release of text-stats.
```

Before it merges, `release:verify` passes for the new tag:

```console
$ git commit -qam "release: v0.1.1" && .mise/tasks/release/verify v0.1.1
ok    tag        0.1.1, newer than v0.1.0
ok    changelog  CHANGELOG.md has the section
$ git switch -q main && git merge -q --squash release-0.1.1 >/dev/null && git commit -qm "release: v0.1.1 (#9)" && git push -q
```

### Tag it by hand

`release-manual.yml` runs `release:manual` with the version. It runs the same
checks as `release:verify`, then tags `main` and pushes the tag, which starts
`release.yml`:

```console
$ .mise/tasks/release/manual 0.1.1
tag       v0.1.1 at 022fc21, pushed
$ .mise/tasks/release/verify v0.1.1 --tagged
ok    tag        0.1.1 at HEAD, newer than v0.1.0
ok    changelog  CHANGELOG.md has the section
$ .mise/tasks/release/notes v0.1.1
### Added

- **python**: count blank lines (#7)

### Deprecated

- `count_words()` is deprecated; use `count()`.

### Fixed

- **python**: count hyphenated words once (#8)

```

`release.yml` builds from the tag:

```console
$ rm -rf dist && python -m build --no-isolation >/dev/null 2>&1 && ls dist
text_stats-0.1.1-py3-none-any.whl
text_stats-0.1.1.tar.gz
$ pip install -q --root-user-action=ignore --no-deps --no-index --target ../site dist/*.whl && PYTHONPATH=../site python -m text_stats --version
text-stats 0.1.1
```

### What release:verify refuses

A version that is not newer than the last release, a version with no changelog
section, and a tag that exists away from `HEAD` all fail:

```console
$ .mise/tasks/release/verify v0.0.9
fail  tag  0.0.9 is not newer than v0.1.1.
[exit 1]
$ .mise/tasks/release/verify v0.3.0
ok    tag        0.3.0, newer than v0.1.1
fail  changelog  CHANGELOG.md has no [0.3.0] section. Run `gitversioned release 0.3.0 --write` and commit it first.
[exit 1]
$ git commit -q --allow-empty -m "docs: typo (#10)" && .mise/tasks/release/verify v0.1.1 --tagged
fail  tag  v0.1.1 already exists at 022fc21, not at HEAD.
[exit 1]
$ .mise/tasks/release/manual 0.1.2
fail  CHANGELOG.md has no [0.1.2] section. Run `gitversioned release 0.1.2 --write` and commit it first.
[exit 1]
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) has no `[tool.gitversioned]` table. The
  defaults are the template's: `v{version}` tags, PEP 440 for Python, the
  `release: vX.Y.Z` title and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `release:verify` is `gitversioned check --tag`: the tag must match the
  template, be newer than the last release, have its `## [X.Y.Z]` section in
  `CHANGELOG.md`, and, if it exists, be at `HEAD`.
- `release:manual` is `gitversioned release VERSION --tag`, which runs the same
  checks before it tags.
- `release:notes` cuts the `## [X.Y.Z]` section out of `CHANGELOG.md` for the
  GitHub release body.
- With the release pull request on, `release-pr.yml` runs `release --pr` and
  `release --tag` instead: see [release-pr](../release-pr/README.md).

## Next

- [template-polyglot](../template-polyglot/README.md) for a render with Rust,
  npm and CITATION.cff.
- [github-actions](../github-actions/README.md) for the workflows that run these
  steps.
````

## File: examples/version-shapes/README.md

````markdown
# Every version shape

Every version gitversioned prints, from one small Python project: releases,
development builds, dirty trees, nightlies and pre-releases, in PEP 440 and in
SemVer, with the settings and environment variables that shape them.

| Level    | Shows                                                       | Needs  |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| Beginner | `version`, `--type`, `--standard`, `--json`, `-C`, `dev`, `nightly`, `date`, `local`, `fallback` | Python |

## Run

Copy this folder anywhere and run the commands below in it. The transcript is
checked on every test run, so it is exactly what you will see, apart from
hashes and dates.

### Before the first tag

A repository with no release tag yet uses the fallback, `0.1.0`, as the base of
a development version. `check` reports it.

```console
$ git init -q && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: first version"
$ gitversioned version
0.1.0.dev20261125+d49ed04
$ gitversioned check | sed -n '1,2p'
ok    config        defaults
warn  git           no release tags match 'v{version}'; versions start from the fallback 0.1.0.
```

### A release

A clean checkout of a release tag is that release:

```console
$ git tag v1.2.0
$ gitversioned version
1.2.0
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.2.0
```

### Development builds

Each commit after a tag is a development build of the next patch release. The
number is the commit date, so two builds of one commit agree, and the local part
is the short commit hash. Python projects print PEP 440 by default; everything
else prints SemVer.

```console
$ echo "x = 1" > src/shapes/extra.py && git add -A && git commit -qm "feat: add extra"
$ gitversioned version
1.2.1.dev20261125+afe97a0
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.2.1-dev.20261125+afe97a0
```

Uncommitted changes add `.dirty` to the local part:

```console
$ echo "y = 2" >> src/shapes/extra.py
$ gitversioned version
1.2.1.dev20261125+afe97a0.dirty
$ git checkout -q -- src/shapes/extra.py
```

PyPI and npm refuse local parts, so a development upload turns them off:

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__LOCAL=false gitversioned version
1.2.1.dev20261125
```

The base of a development build is the next patch by default. `dev = "minor"`
or `"major"` moves it up, and `dev = "next"` asks the commits, here a `feat`:

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__DEV=minor gitversioned version
1.3.0.dev20261125+afe97a0
$ GITVERSIONED__DEV=next gitversioned version
1.3.0.dev20261125+afe97a0
```

`date = "build"` dates the number by the build instead of the commit
(`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` fixes the build time for reproducible builds):

```console
$ GITVERSIONED__DATE=build SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1798761600 gitversioned version
1.2.1.dev20270101+afe97a0
```

### Nightly builds

A nightly is based on the next release the commits ask for and never carries a
local part, so registries accept it:

```console
$ gitversioned version --type nightly
1.3.0.dev20261125
$ gitversioned version --type nightly --standard semver
1.3.0-nightly.20261125
```

`--type release` prints the version a release of this commit would get, and
`--type dev` forces a development version even on a tag.

```console
$ gitversioned version --type release
1.3.0
```

### Pre-releases

Release candidate tags are read in either spelling, `v1.3.0-rc.1` or
`v1.3.0rc1`. A checkout of one is that pre-release, and builds after it are
development builds of the next candidate, so they sort above it:

```console
$ git tag v1.3.0-rc.1
$ gitversioned version
1.3.0rc1
$ gitversioned version --standard semver
1.3.0-rc.1
$ echo "z = 3" >> src/shapes/extra.py && git commit -qam "fix: tweak extra"
$ gitversioned version
1.3.0rc2.dev20261125+95dd958
```

### For scripts

`--json` prints every field, and `-C` runs as if started in another folder:

```console
$ cd .. && gitversioned version -C version-shapes --json
{
  "version": "1.3.0rc2.dev20261125+95dd958",
  "pep440": "1.3.0rc2.dev20261125+95dd958",
  "semver": "1.3.0-rc.2.dev.20261125+95dd958",
  "type": "dev",
  "prerelease": true,
  "source": "tag",
  "tag": "v1.3.0-rc.1",
  "distance": 1,
  "sha": "95dd958",
  "dirty": false,
  "warnings": [],
  "written": [],
  "next": "1.3.0"
}
```

A tag that looks like a version but does not match the tag template is not
used silently:

```console
$ git init -q ../other && cd ../other && git commit -q --allow-empty -m "feat: start" && git tag 2.0.0
$ cd ../other && gitversioned version
WARNING tag 2.0.0 looks like a version but does not match the tag template 'v{version}'; using fallback 0.1.0. Set `tag` to match them.
0.1.0-dev.20261125+8fd1f5c
```

## How it works

- [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml) is a Hatchling project, so the default
  spelling is PEP 440. There are no gitversioned settings; the variables above
  stand in for keys you could set in `[tool.gitversioned]` instead.
- The [concepts guide](https://markurtz.github.io/git-versioned/guides/concepts/)
  explains the order sources are read in and how bases are chosen.

## Next

- [next-version](../next-version/README.md) for how the next release is chosen.
- [ci-safety](../ci-safety/README.md) for what happens when the history is missing.
````
